elaborations.name: VC2LG2E01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing when German and English are being used in the classroom, for example, ‘sandwiching’ a word by saying it in German, then in English, and then again in German

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: reproducing the sounds and rhythms of German by repeating after and imitating the teacher, through choral repetition or chants

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the different languages spoken by members of the class, and listening to the different sounds and ways of saying common expressions such as ‘Good morning’ or ‘My name is …’

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with sounds that are unique to German, imitating the shape of the teacher’s mouth and the sounds produced

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: singing German songs such as an alphabet song, a counting song or a song that focuses on specific sounds

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating books to illustrate the German alphabet, for example, A = Apfel

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: repeating short German tongue twisters and poems out loud

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the use of diacritics can change the sound of letters: Ä/ä, Ö/ö, Ü/ü

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating posters in small groups, illustrating individual letters, with special attention to diacritics and letters used in German but not English (i.e. Ä/ä, Ö/ö, Ü/ü, ß)

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E01-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: colouring, tracing or copying the letters, colouring outlined words of the focus letters (e.g. Fußball) and adding pictures of their own

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2E02 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: develop oral language skills through exploring and listening to the sounds and patterns of the language
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with German Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the sounds in the German alphabet through rote repetition, songs and grouped words focusing on one sound, paying special attention to the letters that are pronounced differently in German (e.g. f, v, w, j) and vowel combinations (e.g. ie, ei)

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing bingo with sounds, words or phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: sorting flashcards with images and/or words into categories related to, for example, the sounds of different vowels, starting consonants and rhyming pairs

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating short wordlists of words grouped into like sounds and practising saying the words, noticing similarities in sounds and spelling

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: clapping the number of syllables in common words, for example, Mor-gen has 2 syllables, Tag has one

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the intonation patterns and understanding the difference between statements, questions and exclamations, for example, Du bist 6 Jahre alt. / Bist du 6 Jahre alt? / Du bist 6 Jahre alt!

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: transforming simple statements into questions by raising the pitch of their voice at the end, for example, Er mag Schokolade. / Er mag Schokolade?

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: walking around the classroom, greeting each other by shaking hands (a standard gesture upon meeting someone in a German-speaking country), asking for the other person’s name, and giving their own name

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: making a class video in which each student introduces themselves in German

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E02-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing Schnipp-Schnapp, the German version of the card game snap, by slapping their own card pile and saying ‘Schnapp’ when their card matches another person’s card – the fastest player takes both piles; if a player makes an incorrect call, their pile goes into the middle – when someone’s card matches the middle card, all players can call ‘Schnipp’ to gain both piles; if a card matches both another player’s and the middle card, all players can call ‘Schnipp-Schnapp’ to gain the matching piles

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2E03 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and respond to greetings, instructions and language relating to their personal world using one- or 2-word responses and/or single-idea phrases
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with German Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and responding to classroom instructions by playing Simon sagt with classroom instructions

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: singing the action song ‘Kopf, Schulter, Knie und Fuß’

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: answering common questions in a variety of contexts, for example, the teacher asks the class; the teacher asks individual students; the students ask a peer; and the students listen to a recording of questions, and speak or record their answers, for example, Wie heißt du? Ich heiße Tom / Ich bin Tom / Mein Name ist Tom; Wo wohnst du? Ich wohne in Ballarat; Wie alt bist du? Ich bin fünf Jahre alt.

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling the 3 forms of ‘the’ (der, die, das) by tracing dotted outlines or copying modelled language to create labels, and then using these to label classroom furniture (e.g. der Stuhl, der Tisch) and fixtures (e.g. der Fußboden, die Tür, das Fenster)

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing memory games that match words with pictures, based on target vocabulary such as simple classroom instructions and phrases, or classroom furniture

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: repeating common phrases such as greetings in response to the teacher’s greeting or prompt, for example, Guten Morgen; Guten Tag

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E03-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: stating, selecting or writing greetings appropriate for the time of day as guided by images, for example, Guten Morgen for a sunrise picture; Gute Nacht for a picture showing the moon and stars

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E03-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using gestures to demonstrate understanding of given greetings for different times of day, for example, stretching and yawning to signify waking up, or putting joined hands together on their cheek and tilting the head to signal going to bed

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E03-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: following common classroom instructions, supported by visual cues displayed in the classroom, for example, Bücher raus; Setz dich hin

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2E04 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: explore connections between language and culture through play and/or imagination
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with German Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using gestures, facial expressions and body language through games such as charades, or by incorporating them into stories, plays or songs to enhance meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing and engaging with cultural items from German-speaking countries, such as euros, postcards and authentic items

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying different parts of an item of Tracht (traditional costume); understanding the basic historical influences of Tracht (e.g. the Dirndl from the alpine regions of Bavaria in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, and South Tyrol in Italy has an apron because it was worn for work, and the apron protects the skirt from stains and dirt); watching videos about different Trachten, pasting pictures of each one onto a map of German-speaking countries and regions, and then displaying the map on the classroom wall or in their books; watching music videos of German-language singers in Tracht and discussing where they are likely to be from, based on their traditional costume

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching pictures to a word and category and discussing the clues found in compound words, for example, types of bread such as Brezel, Semmel, Brötchen, Brot, belegtes Brot, Schinkenbrot and Käsebrot

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a circular diagram of German seasons, copying or pasting the German names of the months within each season, and then decorating each section of the diagram with typical activities associated with that season, for example, snow and ice-skates for winter (Dezember, Januar, Februar)

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating an advent calendar or a class calendar with festivities from German-speaking countries occurring in particular months; participating in and reflecting on activities that demonstrate how German children celebrate various festivals, such as dyeing hard-boiled eggs for Easter and creating an Easter tree (2D on paper or 3D with twigs); receiving lollies and chocolate in their polished shoes on 6 December, Sankt Nikolaustag; or baking Christmas cookies as a class, using simple instructions and target vocabulary in German

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching videos of traditional dancing, for example, the Schuhplattler from southern Germany and Austria, maypole dances for spring festivals and Maitag; learning the history and culture of the dances; learning Germanic folk dances with simple steps

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: labelling pictures of flora and fauna and identifying animals and plants from German-speaking countries

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E04-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing memory games that match words with pictures, based on target vocabulary concerning culture, such as animals (der Wolf), plants (das Edelweiß) and traditional costumes (die Tracht) from German-speaking countries

elaborations.name: VC2LG2E04-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: taste-testing different pretzel flavours (e.g. plain, plain with rock salt, chocolate-coated, cheesy), rating them on a continuum of how delicious they are, and then collating the responses in a simple pictograph

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2C01 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: communicate using formulaic and modelled language relating to aspects of their personal world

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to Wie geht’s? with a variety of expressions (e.g. Mir geht’s gut; Mir geht’s nicht so gut; Ich bin glücklich/müde), as they enter the classroom or during a ‘one-minute challenge’ classroom activity (e.g. greeting as many people in German as they can in one minute)

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in verbal exchange, practising turn-taking using formulaic questions and sentence starters, for example, Wo wohnst du? Ich wohne in Melbourne.

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: following, creating, presenting or recording simple scripts in pairs, asking and answering questions about their name and age, where they live, their siblings and pets, and other modelled language relating to aspects of their personal world

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using puppets or printouts from popular shows or cartoons to role-play greetings and exchange information, imagining themselves as the character

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting and sharing simple expressions and songs with friends and family, for example, singing ‘Zum Geburtstag viel Glück’ and using appropriate greetings (e.g. Hallo!; Guten Abend!; Herzlichen Glückwünsch!) for different times and occasions

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: naming family members and friends and noticing the difference between the formal and informal such as Mama/Mutter and Oma/Großmutter

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using PowerPoint slides or image flashcards to show different pictures (using taught vocabulary) to elicit responses, creating and recording simple scripts in pairs, asking and answering questions about name, age, where they live, siblings, pets, and using other modelled language relating to aspects of their personal world

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2C02 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in a range of guided language activities using formulaic expressions, and visual and spoken cues

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising vocabulary, for example, practising high-frequency verbs using flashcards with images and/or written words, and using gestures to accompany the verbs where appropriate

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing simple memory games (e.g. Ich gehe einkaufen und ich kaufe … to practise vocabulary for fruit and vegetable names), or playing cards to match words or phrases with images

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching simple verbal or written statements to the relevant pictures, for example, Ich bin Maria and Ich bin zehn Jahre alt, matched to the picture of a girl

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching physical or electronic flashcards of questions to their appropriate answers

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: illustrating question-and-answer pairs to demonstrate the meaning of the content

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing fill-the-gap activities based on aural clues

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a scaffold to interchange sentence content (e.g. Ich mag Obst/Schokolade/Wasser), and using accompanying images to make concrete connections

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2C03 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate key information in a variety of texts with support, and respond using gestures, images, words and/or formulaic phrases
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching English and German translations of formulaic questions and answers about their personal world, for example, Wie heißt du? Ich heiße … / Ich bin … / Mein Name ist …; Wie alt bist du? Ich bin … Jahre alt.

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying words in a variety of texts by matching images with words, for example, reading texts with pictograms to facilitate understanding of difficult or previously unseen words

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to scaffolded questions in audiovisual texts using gestures, images, words and/or formulaic phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and/or viewing information presented in an audio or video recording, sequencing key information or writing the topics in order

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: inserting provided answers into cloze or information-gap activities

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: categorising simple metalanguage, for example, identifying and illustrating verbs in a text such as a simple story

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C03-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to texts by sequencing pictures and simple text in the order that the events occurred, or by creating a storyboard to retell a story or information

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C03-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying nouns in simple English and German stories, and then illustrating the nouns to provide a pictorial representation of the story

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2C04 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: explore and make meaning from sounds, words and phrases for familiar objects or terms in German through play, and discover how languages influence each other
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and comparing familiar onomatopoeia in German and English, and then making the relevant noise when their teacher says the name of the animal, or listening to recordings of animals and saying their names in German

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that languages have loan words and that many German words are used in English (e.g. kindergarten) by creating a categories chart to list words from different languages, or playing a sorting game to sort words into their language of origin

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing Hatschi Patschi (each round can have a time/question limit), where one student asks Wie heißt du? to their classmates to identify the 3 to 5 students who were chosen as Hatschi Patschi for that round while the student was out of the room; other students reply with their own names; and students have the option to answer with various sentence starters (e.g. Ich heiße …; Ich bin …; Mein Name ist …)

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching pictures of people to statements to create a ‘family’ or group of friends, for example, Er ist fünfzig Jahre alt, matched to a picture of a man/father

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing pictures of people and saying or writing simple statements about them, using modelled phrases

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2C05 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using words, familiar phrases and modelled language

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C05-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing cloze or information-gap activities by filling in the gaps of a conversation with words, familiar phrases and modelled language

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C05-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording provided or created conversations, asking and answering questions about various topics related to their personal world using modelled language, for example, their name and age, where they live, and their siblings and pets

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C05-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a comic strip where characters ask and answer questions about their name and age, where they live, their siblings and pets, and using other modelled language relating to their personal world

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C05-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a poster or profile about themselves using words, familiar phrases and modelled language, for example, Ich stelle mich vor; Ich mag…

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C05-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating simple statements about people in a picture, using modelled phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C05-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cognates in English and German (e.g. fair – fair) to create original sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LG2C05-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: making simple evaluative statements about their favourite characters in stories, rhythms or songs, for example, Die Geschichte ist toll!; Ich mag Rotkäppchen!; Sie ist freundlich!

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2U01 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: imitate the pronunciation and intonation of spoken German, and understand how sounds are produced

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and contrasting the sounds of individual letters in English and German

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: putting a hand on their throat to identify voice-box vibrations associated with voiced (e.g. b, p) and unvoiced (e.g. t, k) consonants

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the sound of the Umlaut letters (ä, ö, ü) through identifying that these sounds come from the front and top of the mouth, whereas other vowels (a, o, u) come from the back of the throat

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the facial movements involved with making sound blends in German, especially with vowel sounds (e.g. ei in drei)

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the ‘ch’ sound by identifying how ch is pronounced in different German-speaking regions and communities and listening to modelled examples

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying that ch at the end of a word is pronounced much more strongly than ch at the beginning or in the middle of a word; revising this by sorting flashcards into 2 piles based on spelling and/or pronunciation; and then practising the words in each pile, emphasising the soft ch by whispering and the harder ch by speaking more loudly

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: copying words with a ‘sh’ sound, which in German are all written as sch, and comparing and contrasting cognates with English spelling (e.g. washing machine – Waschmaschine)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2U02 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify sound combinations to produce simple words, and then an increasing number of frequently used words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the sounds of diphthongs (a double-vowel sound, where the sound changes from the beginning to the end) in German by listening to the beginning and ending vowels at slow speed (e.g. au = ‘aah-ooh’, as in Haus: ‘H-aah-ooh-s’; eu/äu = ‘oh-ee’, as in Häuser: ‘H-oh-ee-s-er’)

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing words and phrases in a variety of texts, for example, emphasising common sounds in alliterative sentences (e.g. Heidi hüpft hoch; Die Siegerin liest eine Liste und singt ein Lied); using cloze or information-gap activities where they insert words from (pictorial and/or written) flashcards, or working in pairs or small groups to produce sentences about a prompt

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing different actions depending on the sound heard, for example, jumping when they hear sch, or crouching when they hear ch

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: singing in a ‘vowel choir’, where they are grouped according to the first vowel of their name, and then guided by the teacher with hand signals to sing high (teacher’s hand above the head), low (teacher’s hand at thigh level), loudly (teacher opens arms and spreads hands wide), softly (teacher draws arms into chest), a continuous note (teacher moves hand through the air in a continuous line), a pulsing note (teacher opens and closes hand) and so on

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common adjectives for colour (e.g. rot, blau, grün, gelb) and size (e.g. groß, klein) in various contexts, such as to describe classroom items

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using frequently used verbs in a variety of contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and underlining rhyming words or graphemes in short texts or poems

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2U03 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and explore how the Roman alphabet and features of language are used to construct meaning in German

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: alphabetising a group of target words by their first letter

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: becoming familiar with the German alphabet, noticing similarities to and differences from English, by singing the alphabet, and discussing similarities and differences in the sounds

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: spelling out German words chunk by chunk to create a full word (e.g. N-a-m-e for Name)

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: arranging individual letters into words, for example, playing a spelling game with target words, racing to spell the word the teacher says with letter cards

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: arranging words into short phrases or sentences

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2U04 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify that written and spoken German has grammatical structures and other language features that may be similar to or different from English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying phrases that can cause confusion, for example, Ich heiße Martin (I am called Martin) contains one verb in the German phrase and 2 in the English phrase, and a common error in translation is Ich bin heiße Martin (I am am called Martin)

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using conjugations of the verb ‘to be’ – sein from English, German and/or other languages to match different pronouns (e.g. I am – ich bin; you are – du bist; he/she is – er/sie ist), modelling pronoun–verb agreement; or using pictures to illustrate the different conjugations

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching pronouns to verbs in formulaic phrases using ‘to be’ – sein, through, for example, matching flashcards, labelling pictures or filling in a table in English, German and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a table with 4 columns – English, German, Other languages, Picture (to illustrate meaning) – and then writing translations of the same word in each row, noting language features, and supporting the words by associating them with visual images or categorising them with simple metalanguage, for example, putting flashcards with words/pictures into different piles depending on their part of speech; or identifying verbs in a sentence, and then creating sentences of their own using these verbs

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying nouns in English and German texts, and then highlighting the upper-case letters of the German nouns and contrasting how the nouns are written in both languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: ordering pictures of a story into Beginning – Middle – End, and then writing the main idea underneath the picture or matching sentences from the story to each picture

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: continuing a story by, for example, stating what happens to different characters next or using a timeline to plot additional action before or after the story action

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in conversations about character, plot and setting, labelling key ideas and/or annotating pictures with single words and/or short phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U04-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving opinions about different texts using formulaic language, for example, Ich mag das Buch

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U04-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing short responses, including poetry, for example, writing a poem using one German word for each of the letters of their name

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG2U05 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on how language, culture and identity are interconnected and discuss how German-speaking communities are similar to or different from others
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U05-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing their own use of words, expressions or behaviours that make them who they are, including words from different languages known to the class and ways of celebrating or talking that may not be familiar to other people

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U05-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to the ways a word is said in different dialects (e.g. ich is pronounced ‘ick’ in Berlin, ‘isch’ in central Germany, ‘i’ in Bavaria and ‘ich’ in northern Germany, and in Switzerland it becomes very guttural, emphasising the ‘ch’ sound), and repeating the different pronunciations

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U05-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: listing German words that have been borrowed from other languages, especially English (e.g. fair), including many information technology (IT) words (e.g. der Computer), and noting differences in pronunciation and intonation between English and German

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U05-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to cognates in English and German (e.g. April – April) to identify differences in intonation (i.e. which syllables are emphasised), and vowel and consonant sounds

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U05-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how local names of streets, places and landmarks can have their origins in language(s) of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying the meanings of these place names, for example, ‘You Yangs’ comes from the Wadawurrung words Wurdi Youang, meaning ‘big hill’, and then discussing the German names of landforms that also denote physical characteristics, such as der Schwarzwald

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LG2U06-E05 - German

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 3 and 4, German language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences with language. Students communicate and work in collaboration with their peers and teachers through purposeful and creative play in structured activities that involve listening, speaking, reading, writing and viewing. They use German to interact with their peers and teachers and to participate in activities in familiar settings that reflect their interests and capabilities. They use local and digital resources to explore German-speaking communities. They continue to receive extensive support through modelling, scaffolding and repetition, as well as the use of targeted resources.

Students develop active listening skills and use gestures, words and modelled expressions, imitating the sounds, pronunciation and intonation of German. They locate information, and respond to and create texts using written and spoken German. They access authentic and purpose-developed German-language texts such as picture books, stories, songs, digital and animated games, timetables, recipes and advertisements. They recognise the interconnected nature of language, culture and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 4, students use German to initiate structured interactions and share information related to the classroom and their personal worlds. They use modelled language to participate in spoken and written activities. They locate and respond to key items of information in texts, using strategies to help interpret and convey meaning in familiar contexts. They use modelled language and basic grammatical structures to create texts.

Students imitate the sound combinations and rhythms of spoken German. They demonstrate their understanding that German has non-verbal, spoken and written language conventions and rules to convey meaning. They recognise that some terms have cultural meanings. They identify patterns in German and make comparisons between German and English, using simple metalanguage. They understand how aspects of language and culture contribute to their own and others’ identity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4C01 - German
content_descriptions.text: initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about themselves, others and the classroom environment, using formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: communicating with their peers and the teacher using formal and informal simple greetings and formulaic expressions, for example, Wie geht’s?; Wie geht es Ihnen?

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information in modelled expressions in written or spoken form about their family, hometown, pets and activities, for example, Hast du Geschwister? Ich habe einen Bruder und zwei Schwestern.; Hast du ein Haustier? Wir haben einen Hund und vier Vögel.; Wo wohnst du? Ich wohne in …; Was sind deine Hobbys? Ich mag …

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using German expressions and repair strategies to support interaction with their peers and the teacher, for example, Ich verstehe; Ich weiß das nicht; Langsamer bitte; Nochmal bitte

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions relating to a learning activity or lesson, for example, Wie bitte?; Ich verstehe das nicht; Welche Seite?; Wie sagt man das auf Deutsch?; Bist du fertig?; Wer ist dran? Ich bin dran.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled sentences to communicate about the self in descriptive language, for example, Ich habe eine Katze. Sie ist braun und frisst Fleisch.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common responses to frequently asked questions, imitating modelled intonation and stress patterns, for example, Wie geht’s? Gut, danke.; Stimmt das? Ja, das stimmt.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: commenting constructively on their own and others’ learning, for example, Super!; Tolle Arbeit!; Gut gemacht!; Danke.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: apologising and making polite requests, including attracting attention and asking for assistance and permission, for example, Entschuldigung, Frau Lenz!; Hilfe bitte!; Darf ich bitte auf dieToilette gehen?

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions relating to concepts such as time, number, days of the week, months and seasons, for example, Wann spielst du Basketball? Am Montag.; Wer hat im August Geburtstag?; Welche Hobbys hast du?; Wann ist es kalt in Deutschland? Im Dezember, im Winter.

content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve expressing interests and exchanging information, using a range of familiar phrases and modelled structures

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in role-played situations such as choosing a present for a friend or visiting a doctor’s clinic, for example, Alex mag Puppen. Was kostet die Puppe?; Was ist los? Mein Bein tut weh.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating with peers to prepare an item to perform for an audience, for example, a German-language song or a modified fairytale play

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: acting out or providing illustrations for songs or stories (e.g. holding up pictures of each animal as it is mentioned), or creating a stop-motion film narrated by subtitles or purely by the action (e.g. an art gallery of students’ interpretations of Die Bremer Stadtmusikanten)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: making card-matching or digital games to play with peers, using German and English words or images, for example, days of the week, months, seasons or vocabulary associated with weather

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: following procedures and instructions with peers, guided by the teacher, for example, how to create a Hampelmann or Lebkuchenhaus

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating to create a shared text in German, for example, a digital photo story after a class activity or event such as a visit to a German restaurant

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting with others to produce classroom signs, for example, Bitte mach die Tür zu!; Hier sind die Scheren/Klebestifte/Stifte!

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning and negotiating with peers to organise a class celebration such as a traditional festival from a German-speaking country or region or an end-of-term class party, for example, Wer bringt was mit? Ich bringe … mit.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing class games, such as listening to, then repeating, answers from previous students, and then adding their own sentence using specific structures guided by flashcards, for example, Was bringst du zur Party? Peter bringt Brot. Elsa bringt Salat und ich bringe Fisch.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4U02 - German
content_descriptions.text: recognise and use modelled language, formulaic phrases, simple grammatical structures and language conventions to convey meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing sentences that start with formulaic sentence starters, for example, adding an adjective to Der Apfel ist …

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching question-and-answer pairs to create simple conversations, for example, Wo wohnst du? Ich wohne in Shepparton.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying punctuation in modelled writing activities, for example, full stops, exclamation marks and question marks

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: gaining an awareness of terms referring to quantities such as mehr, viel/e, nichts and kein/e, using singular and plural countable nouns (e.g. ein Apfel, viele Äpfel), and uncountable nouns (e.g. Wasser, Orangensaft) to demonstrate understanding

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that all German nouns start with upper-case letters, demonstrating understanding by highlighting nouns within a text

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying capitalisation when writing German nouns

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting German nouns to their articles and recognising that the article applies to the concept of the noun rather than to an individual item

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that genders are used with nouns but not with other parts of speech

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that indefinite/definite articles and possessive adjectives agree with the gender of the noun they precede, for example, der Bruder, ein Bruder, mein Bruder and dein Bruder

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some adverbs to elaborate on simple statements, for example, Ich laufe schnell; Ich singe leise; Ich spreche laut

elaborations.elaboration_text: learning or revising target vocabulary by participating in a Schnitzeljagd in the schoolyard or creating an alphabet list or book with illustrations in German, for example, featuring traditions and customs from German-speaking countries and regions (e.g. L = Lederhosen), or a single topic such as animals (e.g. L = Löwe)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and illustrating short personal, imaginative or informative texts, such as using secure digital tools to produce Mein Traumhaus, and annotating the presentation, for example, Mein Alltag; Mein Schloss ist sehr alt, groß und schön; Es ist rosa und lila

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and/or sharing an item (e.g. Schultüte or Zuckertüte) relating to German-speaking communities’ language and culture through the school newsletter, at a school assembly or in a display, or displaying links to digitally produced student items such as films or photo–text collages

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing simple written correspondence such as invitations or greeting cards in print or digital form, incorporating formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences, and modelled textual conventions, for example, an invitation to Grandparents’ Day at school

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing and presenting illustrated or multimodal texts using a modelled structure, for example, an acrostic poem based on their given name or an Elfchen (an 11-word poem with a specific structure) about a family member or pet

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled structures and picture prompts to retell the basic plot of a narrative or make simple summary statements, for example, Der König und die Königin sind im Schloss

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and presenting a performance using modelled German language, for example, a puppet play involving die Maus from Die Sendung mit der Maus, meeting a current Australian fictional character, or an Igel meeting an echidna

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: acting out a text with a repetitive plot and/or dialogue, and adapting aspects of the story, for example, Die kleine Raupe Nimmersatt or another well-known story from German-speaking countries or regions, noting cultural references (e.g. a bread roll is called die Semmel in Bavaria or Austria, das Brötchen in northern Germany, das Rundstück in Hamburg and Schleswig-Holstein, and die Schrippe in Berlin and Brandenburg)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4C03 - German
content_descriptions.text: locate and respond to key information related to familiar content obtained from spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying points of information with some unfamiliar language in short spoken texts in German, for example, the name and number on a recorded phone message, the age of a child in an interview, or items on a recorded shopping list

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing a timeline of the main events of a story using pictures, words and/or simple sentences or working with information to create a graph, for example, Lieblingstiere, Lieblingssport, Lieblingsserie, Lieblingsmusik

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to an informative or imaginative text in various ways, such as describing what emotions they feel while listening to a story or song, for example, Das macht mich glücklich/traurig/nervös

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting information from informative texts and creating a display with names and appropriate adjectives, for example, reading or listening to texts about different animal species (e.g. Der Löwe ist mutig und stark; Das Känguru ist schnell) and creating a classroom display with the information

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing wall calendars from a German-speaking country and Australia, identifying similarities or differences in structure, public holidays, the pictorial representation of seasons, and cultural influences

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key information in audio or written texts, for example, listening to and/or viewing a song or music video and identifying the number or types of animals or the activities someone completes; or viewing a film poster and reflecting on their understanding using the ‘see-think-wonder’ routine, for example, identifying the title and characters, predicting the genre of the film, and then discussing or presenting this information

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing or listening to texts related to aspects of school life, such as timetables, canteen menus, extracurricular activities and sports, and comparing information about activities and practices across cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating information about a person or character from a written or spoken text, to use in a modelled format such as a Steckbrief

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: working in groups to obtain and use factual information from texts related to other learning areas, for example, completing a simple science experiment, naming countries and significant land features, or calculating distances/speeds from a sports lesson

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding examples of German used at home or in the community and creating a class collection or display, for example, products, labels or words used in English-language advertisements, shop signs, recipe books or menus

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E11 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: classifying a range of German texts (e.g. fairytales, recipes, instructions, advertisements, greeting cards, maps or songs), according to their purpose(s) (e.g. to entertain, describe or instruct), and discussing and justifying their reasoning in English; comparing the features of different types of German and English texts such as a song, picture book, cookbook or comic, and identifying how different textual elements such as title, layout, script and images can combine to make meaning

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4C04 - German
content_descriptions.text: develop strategies to comprehend and produce German, adjusting language to convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning to use a dictionary to find and understand unknown words in texts, for example, playing dictionary games to locate target words

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and comparing similarities and differences between ways of showing politeness or formality in German and English or other languages known to students, for example, the use of family names after Frau and Herr; responding to Danke schön with Bitte schön; using Sie in an appropriate context

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading simple texts in German and English alongside their translations, noticing similarities and differences, and identifying challenges to translations such as ‘false friends’ (e.g. das Handy = mobile phone)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that there are different and/or multiple words that communicate ideas across cultures, for example, Karneval, Fasching and Fastnacht; das Christkind and der Weihnachtsmann

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different words with the same meaning in English, noting subtle variations in meaning (e.g. sidewalk, footpath and pavement; hiking, tramping and trekking) and similar patterns in German (e.g. süß, niedlich and hübsch)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching parallel expressions in English and German, for example, Hi – Tag; morning tea – Kaffeepause; Bless you – Gesundheit

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cultural gestures in familiar contexts, for example, starting with your thumb when counting in German

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discovering how their own language use influences expectations about German-language use, for example, wanting to use one word for ‘you’, and not expecting to capitalise all nouns

content_descriptions.text: initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about themselves, others and the classroom environment, using formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: communicating with their peers and the teacher using formal and informal simple greetings and formulaic expressions, for example, Wie geht’s?; Wie geht es Ihnen?

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information in modelled expressions in written or spoken form about their family, hometown, pets and activities, for example, Hast du Geschwister? Ich habe einen Bruder und zwei Schwestern.; Hast du ein Haustier? Wir haben einen Hund und vier Vögel.; Wo wohnst du? Ich wohne in …; Was sind deine Hobbys? Ich mag …

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using German expressions and repair strategies to support interaction with their peers and the teacher, for example, Ich verstehe; Ich weiß das nicht; Langsamer bitte; Nochmal bitte

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions relating to a learning activity or lesson, for example, Wie bitte?; Ich verstehe das nicht; Welche Seite?; Wie sagt man das auf Deutsch?; Bist du fertig?; Wer ist dran? Ich bin dran.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled sentences to communicate about the self in descriptive language, for example, Ich habe eine Katze. Sie ist braun und frisst Fleisch.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common responses to frequently asked questions, imitating modelled intonation and stress patterns, for example, Wie geht’s? Gut, danke.; Stimmt das? Ja, das stimmt.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: commenting constructively on their own and others’ learning, for example, Super!; Tolle Arbeit!; Gut gemacht!; Danke.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: apologising and making polite requests, including attracting attention and asking for assistance and permission, for example, Entschuldigung, Frau Lenz!; Hilfe bitte!; Darf ich bitte auf dieToilette gehen?

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions relating to concepts such as time, number, days of the week, months and seasons, for example, Wann spielst du Basketball? Am Montag.; Wer hat im August Geburtstag?; Welche Hobbys hast du?; Wann ist es kalt in Deutschland? Im Dezember, im Winter.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4C02 - German
content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve expressing interests and exchanging information, using a range of familiar phrases and modelled structures

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in role-played situations such as choosing a present for a friend or visiting a doctor’s clinic, for example, Alex mag Puppen. Was kostet die Puppe?; Was ist los? Mein Bein tut weh.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating with peers to prepare an item to perform for an audience, for example, a German-language song or a modified fairytale play

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: acting out or providing illustrations for songs or stories (e.g. holding up pictures of each animal as it is mentioned), or creating a stop-motion film narrated by subtitles or purely by the action (e.g. an art gallery of students’ interpretations of Die Bremer Stadtmusikanten)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: making card-matching or digital games to play with peers, using German and English words or images, for example, days of the week, months, seasons or vocabulary associated with weather

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: following procedures and instructions with peers, guided by the teacher, for example, how to create a Hampelmann or Lebkuchenhaus

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating to create a shared text in German, for example, a digital photo story after a class activity or event such as a visit to a German restaurant

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting with others to produce classroom signs, for example, Bitte mach die Tür zu!; Hier sind die Scheren/Klebestifte/Stifte!

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning and negotiating with peers to organise a class celebration such as a traditional festival from a German-speaking country or region or an end-of-term class party, for example, Wer bringt was mit? Ich bringe … mit.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing class games, such as listening to, then repeating, answers from previous students, and then adding their own sentence using specific structures guided by flashcards, for example, Was bringst du zur Party? Peter bringt Brot. Elsa bringt Salat und ich bringe Fisch.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4C05 - German
content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts using formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences, and modelled textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning or revising target vocabulary by participating in a Schnitzeljagd in the schoolyard or creating an alphabet list or book with illustrations in German, for example, featuring traditions and customs from German-speaking countries and regions (e.g. L = Lederhosen), or a single topic such as animals (e.g. L = Löwe)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and illustrating short personal, imaginative or informative texts, such as using secure digital tools to produce Mein Traumhaus, and annotating the presentation, for example, Mein Alltag; Mein Schloss ist sehr alt, groß und schön; Es ist rosa und lila

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and/or sharing an item (e.g. Schultüte or Zuckertüte) relating to German-speaking communities’ language and culture through the school newsletter, at a school assembly or in a display, or displaying links to digitally produced student items such as films or photo–text collages

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing simple written correspondence such as invitations or greeting cards in print or digital form, incorporating formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences, and modelled textual conventions, for example, an invitation to Grandparents’ Day at school

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing and presenting illustrated or multimodal texts using a modelled structure, for example, an acrostic poem based on their given name or an Elfchen (an 11-word poem with a specific structure) about a family member or pet

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled structures and picture prompts to retell the basic plot of a narrative or make simple summary statements, for example, Der König und die Königin sind im Schloss

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and presenting a performance using modelled German language, for example, a puppet play involving die Maus from Die Sendung mit der Maus, meeting a current Australian fictional character, or an Igel meeting an echidna

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: acting out a text with a repetitive plot and/or dialogue, and adapting aspects of the story, for example, Die kleine Raupe Nimmersatt or another well-known story from German-speaking countries or regions, noting cultural references (e.g. a bread roll is called die Semmel in Bavaria or Austria, das Brötchen in northern Germany, das Rundstück in Hamburg and Schleswig-Holstein, and die Schrippe in Berlin and Brandenburg)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4U02 - German
content_descriptions.text: recognise and use modelled language, formulaic phrases, simple grammatical structures and language conventions to convey meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing sentences that start with formulaic sentence starters, for example, adding an adjective to Der Apfel ist …

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching question-and-answer pairs to create simple conversations, for example, Wo wohnst du? Ich wohne in Shepparton.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying punctuation in modelled writing activities, for example, full stops, exclamation marks and question marks

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: gaining an awareness of terms referring to quantities such as mehr, viel/e, nichts and kein/e, using singular and plural countable nouns (e.g. ein Apfel, viele Äpfel), and uncountable nouns (e.g. Wasser, Orangensaft) to demonstrate understanding

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that all German nouns start with upper-case letters, demonstrating understanding by highlighting nouns within a text

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying capitalisation when writing German nouns

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting German nouns to their articles and recognising that the article applies to the concept of the noun rather than to an individual item

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that genders are used with nouns but not with other parts of speech

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that indefinite/definite articles and possessive adjectives agree with the gender of the noun they precede, for example, der Bruder, ein Bruder, mein Bruder and dein Bruder

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some adverbs to elaborate on simple statements, for example, Ich laufe schnell; Ich singe leise; Ich spreche laut

as_extracts.name: LGERF104-E05
as_extracts.description: Students imitate the sound combinations and rhythms of spoken German.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4U01 - German
content_descriptions.text: recognise sound combinations, and use patterns of pronunciation and intonation to form words, phrases and simple sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using the Umlaut and Eszett to pronounce and write familiar German words, noting differences in their pronunciation, for example, words with and without an Umlaut (e.g. der Bruder vs. die Brüder)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing pronunciation, phrasing and intonation skills by singing, reciting poetry or reading a short text aloud

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and practising sounds in German that are different from English sounds, for example, Wasser, where w sounds like an English ‘v’; Vater, where v sounds like an English ‘f’; other words such as ja, rot, singen, Sport and zwei

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that intonation patterns create different meanings between statements, questions and exclamations, for example, Du bist acht. / Du bist acht? / Du bist acht!

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying differences in regional accents and dialects to begin understanding language variation across German-speaking communities, for example, in everyday greetings

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the rhythms and vocal effects in German and English versions of a favourite story such as ‘Rotkäppchen’ or in a game such as Wie spät ist es Herr Wolf?

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using phonic knowledge to spell and write some unfamiliar words containing, for example, ch, r, th, u and z, and consonant clusters such as sch

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying learned memory aids such as ‘When E and I go walking, the second one does the talking’ (e.g. Reise vs. Riese)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying spelling rules for frequently used words

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to the way animal sounds are expressed in German (e.g. in the story ‘Die Bremer Stadtmusikanten’ or the song ‘Das kleine Küken piept’) and comparing them with English and other languages represented within the class, for example, Ein Hahn sagt: „kikeriki“; Ein Hund bellt: „wau wau“

as_extracts.name: LGERF104-E06
as_extracts.description: They demonstrate their understanding that German has non-verbal, spoken and written language conventions and rules to convey meaning.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4C04 - German
content_descriptions.text: develop strategies to comprehend and produce German, adjusting language to convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning to use a dictionary to find and understand unknown words in texts, for example, playing dictionary games to locate target words

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and comparing similarities and differences between ways of showing politeness or formality in German and English or other languages known to students, for example, the use of family names after Frau and Herr; responding to Danke schön with Bitte schön; using Sie in an appropriate context

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading simple texts in German and English alongside their translations, noticing similarities and differences, and identifying challenges to translations such as ‘false friends’ (e.g. das Handy = mobile phone)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that there are different and/or multiple words that communicate ideas across cultures, for example, Karneval, Fasching and Fastnacht; das Christkind and der Weihnachtsmann

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different words with the same meaning in English, noting subtle variations in meaning (e.g. sidewalk, footpath and pavement; hiking, tramping and trekking) and similar patterns in German (e.g. süß, niedlich and hübsch)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching parallel expressions in English and German, for example, Hi – Tag; morning tea – Kaffeepause; Bless you – Gesundheit

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cultural gestures in familiar contexts, for example, starting with your thumb when counting in German

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discovering how their own language use influences expectations about German-language use, for example, wanting to use one word for ‘you’, and not expecting to capitalise all nouns

elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a map that shows Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages and noticing how many languages are represented in Victoria, and then learning about the diversity of languages that students in the classroom have a connection to

elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country on which they live and naming this in German, and incorporating this into their self-introduction

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1

organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a ‘language portrait’ of themselves through the use of a whole-body silhouette, where students represent their personal experiences of language and culture by adding colours, shapes and words within and around the outline

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that language carries cultural ideas, for example, Sommerbeginn, which is officially 1 December in Australia but 21 or 22 June in Europe; hitzefrei, or ‘heat-free’, referring to the practice of dismissing students early from school if a certain temperature is reached or forecast

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring cultural practices and language related to foods in German-speaking countries and regions, for example, Abendbrot and Spaghettieis, or saying Guten appetit before a meal

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying ways in which German language and culture influence the lives of Australians, for example, types of food consumed such as Sauerkraut, types of sausage, and sweets (e.g. Gummibärchen)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that politeness and formality may be communicated differently in different languages, for example, the use of Frau/Herr Schmidt (Ms/Mr Smith) and the use of du/Sie to indicate the level of formality between speakers in German-speaking communities

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that German is the official language or a co-official language of multiple countries and regions, including Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Belgium, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, and South Tyrol in Italy, and identifying their locations on a world map

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning about the school system in German-speaking countries, where the Grundschule is generally for Grades 1 to 4

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: illustrating mythical creatures from different cultures based on verbal and/or written descriptions

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E11 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising character traits and values and comparing them with familiar stories in English or in other languages, for example, the wolf in ‘Rotkäppchen’ as told by the Brothers Grimm in German compared to popular retellings of ‘Little Red Riding Hood’

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E12 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that some English words originate from Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander languages, such as the names of animals (e.g. ‘koala’ – der Koala from the Dharug word gula meaning ‘no water’; ‘kangaroo’ – das Känguru from the Guugu Yimithirr word gangurru), comparing them to the German words and discussing why more Australian animal words come from some areas than others

as_extracts.name: LGERF104-E08
as_extracts.description: They identify patterns in German and make comparisons between German and English, using simple metalanguage.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4C04 - German
content_descriptions.text: develop strategies to comprehend and produce German, adjusting language to convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning to use a dictionary to find and understand unknown words in texts, for example, playing dictionary games to locate target words

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and comparing similarities and differences between ways of showing politeness or formality in German and English or other languages known to students, for example, the use of family names after Frau and Herr; responding to Danke schön with Bitte schön; using Sie in an appropriate context

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading simple texts in German and English alongside their translations, noticing similarities and differences, and identifying challenges to translations such as ‘false friends’ (e.g. das Handy = mobile phone)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that there are different and/or multiple words that communicate ideas across cultures, for example, Karneval, Fasching and Fastnacht; das Christkind and der Weihnachtsmann

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different words with the same meaning in English, noting subtle variations in meaning (e.g. sidewalk, footpath and pavement; hiking, tramping and trekking) and similar patterns in German (e.g. süß, niedlich and hübsch)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching parallel expressions in English and German, for example, Hi – Tag; morning tea – Kaffeepause; Bless you – Gesundheit

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cultural gestures in familiar contexts, for example, starting with your thumb when counting in German

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discovering how their own language use influences expectations about German-language use, for example, wanting to use one word for ‘you’, and not expecting to capitalise all nouns

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4U01 - German
content_descriptions.text: recognise sound combinations, and use patterns of pronunciation and intonation to form words, phrases and simple sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using the Umlaut and Eszett to pronounce and write familiar German words, noting differences in their pronunciation, for example, words with and without an Umlaut (e.g. der Bruder vs. die Brüder)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing pronunciation, phrasing and intonation skills by singing, reciting poetry or reading a short text aloud

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and practising sounds in German that are different from English sounds, for example, Wasser, where w sounds like an English ‘v’; Vater, where v sounds like an English ‘f’; other words such as ja, rot, singen, Sport and zwei

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that intonation patterns create different meanings between statements, questions and exclamations, for example, Du bist acht. / Du bist acht? / Du bist acht!

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying differences in regional accents and dialects to begin understanding language variation across German-speaking communities, for example, in everyday greetings

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the rhythms and vocal effects in German and English versions of a favourite story such as ‘Rotkäppchen’ or in a game such as Wie spät ist es Herr Wolf?

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using phonic knowledge to spell and write some unfamiliar words containing, for example, ch, r, th, u and z, and consonant clusters such as sch

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying learned memory aids such as ‘When E and I go walking, the second one does the talking’ (e.g. Reise vs. Riese)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying spelling rules for frequently used words

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to the way animal sounds are expressed in German (e.g. in the story ‘Die Bremer Stadtmusikanten’ or the song ‘Das kleine Küken piept’) and comparing them with English and other languages represented within the class, for example, Ein Hahn sagt: „kikeriki“; Ein Hund bellt: „wau wau“

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4U03 - German
content_descriptions.text: recognise and compare familiar German language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using simple metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying German punctuation for direct speech by highlighting the speech marks within a text (e.g „Ich bin Heidi.“ or »Ich bin Heidi.«), noting that the »…« formation is commonly found in novels

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating a simple English text featuring direct speech into German, changing English punctuation for direct speech to German punctuation (e.g. He said, ‘I like chocolate.’ becomes Er sagt: „Ich mag Schokolade.“ or Er sagt: »Ich mag Schokolade.«)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the pluralisation of nouns in German to English and/or other languages, for example, der Apfel / die Äpfel

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and using pronouns to refer to people (singular: ich, du, er, sie, es, Sie; plural: wir, ihr, Sie, sie), for example, Sie heißt Anna; Sie heißen Ben und Sarah; Das Baby ist klein. Es schläft.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and matching keywords in German, English and/or other languages, for example, names for German-speaking countries and regions (e.g. Deutschland), well-known cities (e.g. Wien), animals (e.g. der Hund, die Katze), family members (e.g. die Mutter, der Bruder) and leisure activities (e.g. Musik hören, schwimmen)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the features of different types of German, English and/or other language texts such as a song, picture book, cookbook or a comic, and identifying how different textual elements such as title, layout, script and images can combine to make meaning

as_extracts.name: LGERF104-E09
as_extracts.description: They understand how aspects of language and culture contribute to their own and others’ identity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4U04 - German
content_descriptions.text: identify connections between personal identity, language and aspects of culture
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture
