substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4C01 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about themselves, others and the classroom environment, using formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: communicating with their peers and the teacher using formal and informal simple greetings and formulaic expressions, for example, Wie geht’s?; Wie geht es Ihnen?

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information in modelled expressions in written or spoken form about their family, hometown, pets and activities, for example, Hast du Geschwister? Ich habe einen Bruder und zwei Schwestern.; Hast du ein Haustier? Wir haben einen Hund und vier Vögel.; Wo wohnst du? Ich wohne in …; Was sind deine Hobbys? Ich mag …

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using German expressions and repair strategies to support interaction with their peers and the teacher, for example, Ich verstehe; Ich weiß das nicht; Langsamer bitte; Nochmal bitte

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions relating to a learning activity or lesson, for example, Wie bitte?; Ich verstehe das nicht; Welche Seite?; Wie sagt man das auf Deutsch?; Bist du fertig?; Wer ist dran? Ich bin dran.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled sentences to communicate about the self in descriptive language, for example, Ich habe eine Katze. Sie ist braun und frisst Fleisch.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common responses to frequently asked questions, imitating modelled intonation and stress patterns, for example, Wie geht’s? Gut, danke.; Stimmt das? Ja, das stimmt.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: commenting constructively on their own and others’ learning, for example, Super!; Tolle Arbeit!; Gut gemacht!; Danke.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: apologising and making polite requests, including attracting attention and asking for assistance and permission, for example, Entschuldigung, Frau Lenz!; Hilfe bitte!; Darf ich bitte auf dieToilette gehen?

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions relating to concepts such as time, number, days of the week, months and seasons, for example, Wann spielst du Basketball? Am Montag.; Wer hat im August Geburtstag?; Welche Hobbys hast du?; Wann ist es kalt in Deutschland? Im Dezember, im Winter.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4C02 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve expressing interests and exchanging information, using a range of familiar phrases and modelled structures

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in role-played situations such as choosing a present for a friend or visiting a doctor’s clinic, for example, Alex mag Puppen. Was kostet die Puppe?; Was ist los? Mein Bein tut weh.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating with peers to prepare an item to perform for an audience, for example, a German-language song or a modified fairytale play

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: acting out or providing illustrations for songs or stories (e.g. holding up pictures of each animal as it is mentioned), or creating a stop-motion film narrated by subtitles or purely by the action (e.g. an art gallery of students’ interpretations of Die Bremer Stadtmusikanten)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: making card-matching or digital games to play with peers, using German and English words or images, for example, days of the week, months, seasons or vocabulary associated with weather

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: following procedures and instructions with peers, guided by the teacher, for example, how to create a Hampelmann or Lebkuchenhaus

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating to create a shared text in German, for example, a digital photo story after a class activity or event such as a visit to a German restaurant

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting with others to produce classroom signs, for example, Bitte mach die Tür zu!; Hier sind die Scheren/Klebestifte/Stifte!

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning and negotiating with peers to organise a class celebration such as a traditional festival from a German-speaking country or region or an end-of-term class party, for example, Wer bringt was mit? Ich bringe … mit.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing class games, such as listening to, then repeating, answers from previous students, and then adding their own sentence using specific structures guided by flashcards, for example, Was bringst du zur Party? Peter bringt Brot. Elsa bringt Salat und ich bringe Fisch.

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4C03 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate and respond to key information related to familiar content obtained from spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying points of information with some unfamiliar language in short spoken texts in German, for example, the name and number on a recorded phone message, the age of a child in an interview, or items on a recorded shopping list

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing a timeline of the main events of a story using pictures, words and/or simple sentences or working with information to create a graph, for example, Lieblingstiere, Lieblingssport, Lieblingsserie, Lieblingsmusik

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to an informative or imaginative text in various ways, such as describing what emotions they feel while listening to a story or song, for example, Das macht mich glücklich/traurig/nervös

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting information from informative texts and creating a display with names and appropriate adjectives, for example, reading or listening to texts about different animal species (e.g. Der Löwe ist mutig und stark; Das Känguru ist schnell) and creating a classroom display with the information

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing wall calendars from a German-speaking country and Australia, identifying similarities or differences in structure, public holidays, the pictorial representation of seasons, and cultural influences

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key information in audio or written texts, for example, listening to and/or viewing a song or music video and identifying the number or types of animals or the activities someone completes; or viewing a film poster and reflecting on their understanding using the ‘see-think-wonder’ routine, for example, identifying the title and characters, predicting the genre of the film, and then discussing or presenting this information

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing or listening to texts related to aspects of school life, such as timetables, canteen menus, extracurricular activities and sports, and comparing information about activities and practices across cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating information about a person or character from a written or spoken text, to use in a modelled format such as a Steckbrief

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: working in groups to obtain and use factual information from texts related to other learning areas, for example, completing a simple science experiment, naming countries and significant land features, or calculating distances/speeds from a sports lesson

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding examples of German used at home or in the community and creating a class collection or display, for example, products, labels or words used in English-language advertisements, shop signs, recipe books or menus

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C03-E11 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: classifying a range of German texts (e.g. fairytales, recipes, instructions, advertisements, greeting cards, maps or songs), according to their purpose(s) (e.g. to entertain, describe or instruct), and discussing and justifying their reasoning in English; comparing the features of different types of German and English texts such as a song, picture book, cookbook or comic, and identifying how different textual elements such as title, layout, script and images can combine to make meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching parallel expressions in English and German, for example, Hi – Tag; morning tea – Kaffeepause; Bless you – Gesundheit

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cultural gestures in familiar contexts, for example, starting with your thumb when counting in German

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discovering how their own language use influences expectations about German-language use, for example, wanting to use one word for ‘you’, and not expecting to capitalise all nouns

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4C05 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts using formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences, and modelled textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning or revising target vocabulary by participating in a Schnitzeljagd in the schoolyard or creating an alphabet list or book with illustrations in German, for example, featuring traditions and customs from German-speaking countries and regions (e.g. L = Lederhosen), or a single topic such as animals (e.g. L = Löwe)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and illustrating short personal, imaginative or informative texts, such as using secure digital tools to produce Mein Traumhaus, and annotating the presentation, for example, Mein Alltag; Mein Schloss ist sehr alt, groß und schön; Es ist rosa und lila

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and/or sharing an item (e.g. Schultüte or Zuckertüte) relating to German-speaking communities’ language and culture through the school newsletter, at a school assembly or in a display, or displaying links to digitally produced student items such as films or photo–text collages

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing simple written correspondence such as invitations or greeting cards in print or digital form, incorporating formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences, and modelled textual conventions, for example, an invitation to Grandparents’ Day at school

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing and presenting illustrated or multimodal texts using a modelled structure, for example, an acrostic poem based on their given name or an Elfchen (an 11-word poem with a specific structure) about a family member or pet

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled structures and picture prompts to retell the basic plot of a narrative or make simple summary statements, for example, Der König und die Königin sind im Schloss

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and presenting a performance using modelled German language, for example, a puppet play involving die Maus from Die Sendung mit der Maus, meeting a current Australian fictional character, or an Igel meeting an echidna

elaborations.name: VC2LG4C05-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: acting out a text with a repetitive plot and/or dialogue, and adapting aspects of the story, for example, Die kleine Raupe Nimmersatt or another well-known story from German-speaking countries or regions, noting cultural references (e.g. a bread roll is called die Semmel in Bavaria or Austria, das Brötchen in northern Germany, das Rundstück in Hamburg and Schleswig-Holstein, and die Schrippe in Berlin and Brandenburg)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4U01 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise sound combinations, and use patterns of pronunciation and intonation to form words, phrases and simple sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using the Umlaut and Eszett to pronounce and write familiar German words, noting differences in their pronunciation, for example, words with and without an Umlaut (e.g. der Bruder vs. die Brüder)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing pronunciation, phrasing and intonation skills by singing, reciting poetry or reading a short text aloud

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and practising sounds in German that are different from English sounds, for example, Wasser, where w sounds like an English ‘v’; Vater, where v sounds like an English ‘f’; other words such as ja, rot, singen, Sport and zwei

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that intonation patterns create different meanings between statements, questions and exclamations, for example, Du bist acht. / Du bist acht? / Du bist acht!

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying differences in regional accents and dialects to begin understanding language variation across German-speaking communities, for example, in everyday greetings

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the rhythms and vocal effects in German and English versions of a favourite story such as ‘Rotkäppchen’ or in a game such as Wie spät ist es Herr Wolf?

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using phonic knowledge to spell and write some unfamiliar words containing, for example, ch, r, th, u and z, and consonant clusters such as sch

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying learned memory aids such as ‘When E and I go walking, the second one does the talking’ (e.g. Reise vs. Riese)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying spelling rules for frequently used words

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U01-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to the way animal sounds are expressed in German (e.g. in the story ‘Die Bremer Stadtmusikanten’ or the song ‘Das kleine Küken piept’) and comparing them with English and other languages represented within the class, for example, Ein Hahn sagt: „kikeriki“; Ein Hund bellt: „wau wau“

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4U02 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use modelled language, formulaic phrases, simple grammatical structures and language conventions to convey meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: completing sentences that start with formulaic sentence starters, for example, adding an adjective to Der Apfel ist …

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching question-and-answer pairs to create simple conversations, for example, Wo wohnst du? Ich wohne in Shepparton.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying punctuation in modelled writing activities, for example, full stops, exclamation marks and question marks

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: gaining an awareness of terms referring to quantities such as mehr, viel/e, nichts and kein/e, using singular and plural countable nouns (e.g. ein Apfel, viele Äpfel), and uncountable nouns (e.g. Wasser, Orangensaft) to demonstrate understanding

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that all German nouns start with upper-case letters, demonstrating understanding by highlighting nouns within a text

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying capitalisation when writing German nouns

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting German nouns to their articles and recognising that the article applies to the concept of the noun rather than to an individual item

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that genders are used with nouns but not with other parts of speech

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that indefinite/definite articles and possessive adjectives agree with the gender of the noun they precede, for example, der Bruder, ein Bruder, mein Bruder and dein Bruder

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U02-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some adverbs to elaborate on simple statements, for example, Ich laufe schnell; Ich singe leise; Ich spreche laut

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG4U03 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and compare familiar German language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using simple metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying German punctuation for direct speech by highlighting the speech marks within a text (e.g „Ich bin Heidi.“ or »Ich bin Heidi.«), noting that the »…« formation is commonly found in novels

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating a simple English text featuring direct speech into German, changing English punctuation for direct speech to German punctuation (e.g. He said, ‘I like chocolate.’ becomes Er sagt: „Ich mag Schokolade.“ or Er sagt: »Ich mag Schokolade.«)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the pluralisation of nouns in German to English and/or other languages, for example, der Apfel / die Äpfel

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and using pronouns to refer to people (singular: ich, du, er, sie, es, Sie; plural: wir, ihr, Sie, sie), for example, Sie heißt Anna; Sie heißen Ben und Sarah; Das Baby ist klein. Es schläft.

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and matching keywords in German, English and/or other languages, for example, names for German-speaking countries and regions (e.g. Deutschland), well-known cities (e.g. Wien), animals (e.g. der Hund, die Katze), family members (e.g. die Mutter, der Bruder) and leisure activities (e.g. Musik hören, schwimmen)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the features of different types of German, English and/or other language texts such as a song, picture book, cookbook or a comic, and identifying how different textual elements such as title, layout, script and images can combine to make meaning

elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country on which they live and naming this in German, and incorporating this into their self-introduction

elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a ‘language portrait’ of themselves through the use of a whole-body silhouette, where students represent their personal experiences of language and culture by adding colours, shapes and words within and around the outline

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that language carries cultural ideas, for example, Sommerbeginn, which is officially 1 December in Australia but 21 or 22 June in Europe; hitzefrei, or ‘heat-free’, referring to the practice of dismissing students early from school if a certain temperature is reached or forecast

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring cultural practices and language related to foods in German-speaking countries and regions, for example, Abendbrot and Spaghettieis, or saying Guten appetit before a meal

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying ways in which German language and culture influence the lives of Australians, for example, types of food consumed such as Sauerkraut, types of sausage, and sweets (e.g. Gummibärchen)

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that politeness and formality may be communicated differently in different languages, for example, the use of Frau/Herr Schmidt (Ms/Mr Smith) and the use of du/Sie to indicate the level of formality between speakers in German-speaking communities

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that German is the official language or a co-official language of multiple countries and regions, including Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Belgium, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, and South Tyrol in Italy, and identifying their locations on a world map

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning about the school system in German-speaking countries, where the Grundschule is generally for Grades 1 to 4

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: illustrating mythical creatures from different cultures based on verbal and/or written descriptions

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E11 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising character traits and values and comparing them with familiar stories in English or in other languages, for example, the wolf in ‘Rotkäppchen’ as told by the Brothers Grimm in German compared to popular retellings of ‘Little Red Riding Hood’

elaborations.name: VC2LG4U04-E12 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that some English words originate from Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander languages, such as the names of animals (e.g. ‘koala’ – der Koala from the Dharug word gula meaning ‘no water’; ‘kangaroo’ – das Känguru from the Guugu Yimithirr word gangurru), comparing them to the German words and discussing why more Australian animal words come from some areas than others

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 5 and 6, German language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences with language. Students communicate and work in collaboration with their peers and teachers in purposeful, creative and structured activities that involve listening, speaking, reading, writing and viewing. They interact in German to exchange information and ideas within their school and local environment, and engage with German-speaking communities. They work independently and in groups, with ongoing support from modelling and from digital and print resources.

Students engage with a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts that may include stories, posters, images, notes, invitations, video clips and procedural texts. They identify language structures and features of German, and use simple metalanguage to reflect on their understanding. They recognise that some words and expressions are not easily translated, and reflect on how diverse cultural practices, behaviours and values influence communication and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 6, students initiate and use strategies to maintain interactions in German that are related to their immediate environment. They use appropriate sound combinations, intonation and rhythm in spoken texts. They collaborate in spoken and written activities to share information, preferences and ideas. They use strategies to locate and interpret information and ideas in texts, and demonstrate understanding by responding in German or English, adjusting their responses to context, purpose and audience.

Students use modelled structures when creating and responding in German. They create texts, selecting and using a variety of vocabulary and sentence structures to suit different contexts. They use conventions appropriate to text type. They apply rules for pronunciation and intonation in spoken language and apply conventions of spelling and punctuation in written language. They compare language structures and features in German and English, using familiar metalanguage. They show understanding of how language and culture are interconnected and consider how this is reflected in their own language(s), culture(s) and identity.

as_extracts.name: LGERF106-E01
as_extracts.description: students initiate and use strategies to maintain interactions in German that are related to their immediate environment.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6C01 - German
content_descriptions.text: initiate and sustain modelled exchanges in familiar contexts related to their personal worlds and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information with others in a secure, teacher-moderated online environment, in writing or face-to-face, about daily routines and leisure activities, using modelled language associated with time and sequence, for example, Was machst du am Wochenende?; Ich stehe um 7.30 Uhr auf. Dann frühstücke ich.; Ich schwimme und surfe oft; or sharing opinions with German-speaking peers about school subjects and rules, for example, Wie findest du Mathe? Mathe ist toll.; Man muss eine Uniform tragen. Das ist doof. Was denkst du?

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using communication strategies such as active listening skills and interjections (e.g. Ja, ja ich verstehe; Ach ja das stimmt; Genau), turn-taking cues, and requests for clarification or more detail to support interactions (e.g. Ich verstehe das nicht; Wie heißt das auf Englisch?)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising modelled repair strategies, for example, Wie bitte?; Kannst du die Frage nochmal sagen?; Bitte sag das nochmal

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving and receiving instructions, for example, Mach(t) die Tür zu!; Trink(t) mehr Wasser!

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing significant people such as family members, friends and teachers, using simple descriptive and expressive modelled language, for example, Das ist meine Schwester. Sie ist sehr sportlich und intelligent. Sie spielt sehr gern Fußball und liest gern Comics. Ich habe meine Schwester lieb.

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking questions using question words to request further detail, and responding using modelled intonation and stress patterns, for example, Welche Farbe hat dein Haustier?; Wie ist es?; Wo wohnt es?

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising subject–verb inversion of questions (e.g. Er ist zehn Jahre alt / Ist er zehn Jahre alt?)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and discussing learning strengths and experiences, for example, Ich mag Deutsch. Deutsch macht Spaß. Ich lerne gern Deutsch.

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: apologising and expressing concern or sympathy to friends and family members, for example, Tut mir leid; Schade!; Du Arme(r)!

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing feelings (e.g. Wie geht’s?; Es geht mir nicht gut; Ich bin krank), using adjectives such as aufgeregt, glücklich, nervös, sauer and traurig

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6C02 - German
content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve discussion with others, using language that expresses information, preferences and ideas

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in real-life or role-played transactions such as buying food from a range, for example, Ich esse Käse. Ich nehme ein Käsebrötchen.; Was kostet ein Eis? Das macht 6,50 Euro.; Gibt es Vanilla? Vanilla ist mein Lieblingseis.

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising and conducting collaborative activities such as a Deutsch macht fit session for a younger class, using language such as Lauft schnell! and Springt zehnmal!

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing and planning collaboratively with peers to develop an activity for a school assembly, or a school/class event or performance, using language related to people, items, time and numbers to create promotional materials, for example, working collaboratively to produce a poster or video to encourage recycling (e.g. Trinkt lieber Wasser!; Recycelt alle Dosen!) or dancing the action song ‘Das Fliegerlied’ as a lunchtime flash mob

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: checking on peer progress using comments and questions (e.g. Bist du fertig? Ich bin fertig.; Verstehst du das? Ja.) and sharing ideas about the experience of learning and using German, identifying their own strengths and preferred learning styles, for example, Ich kann gut Deutsch sprechen

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to feedback on a written draft or class activity by making changes to improve the product or activity

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: consulting online catalogues and websites, comparing prices and values, and discussing potential purchases (e.g. Das Handy ist zu teuer; Der Pullover ist preiswert) and using modelled phrases such as Der Hut sieht gut aus

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: stating preferences from a range of items, for example, designing outfits from a clothing catalogue (e.g. Mein Lieblingsoutfit ist lila und weiß)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking peers to do something politely and responding to requests, for example, giving and receiving things (e.g. Gib mir bitte den Stift!; Bitte schön; Danke schön)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing and creating class and school rules using modelled language with the modal verbs müssen and dürfen, for example, Dürfen wir auf dem Boden sitzen?; Wir müssen immer aufpassen; Wir dürfen in der Klasse nicht am Handy sein

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the exchange rate of currencies, for example, converting Euro or Schweizer Franken into Australian dollars, and calculating the cost of specific items in both currencies

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6C05 - German
content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, using a variety of vocabulary, modelled sentence structures and conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and highlighting typical features of a letter or article, labelling different sections (e.g. heading, introduction, body, conclusion, author), and then annotating a text to identify its structure and linguistic features

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying features common to a range of text types (e.g. title, author, and main content organised into paragraphs), and then completing a jigsaw activity using features of various text types, placing fragments of the text into the correct order based on modelled examples

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a multimedia profile for a group of young German speakers or writing a blog entry for a youth website, for example, about Freizeit, Schule or Freunde

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a video clip to present information or ideas to a particular audience, including elements that may be unfamiliar to German-speaking students, for example, a virtual tour of the school or classroom for exchange student groups, which may also demonstrate that Australian students generally wear school uniforms

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting about German-speaking countries and Australia, for example, population statistics and physical size, daily temperatures, types of housing, pet ownership or most popular leisure activities

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording a multimedia presentation or writing a diary about a real or imaginary trip to a German-speaking country or region, incorporating some famous places they visited and cultural experiences, for example, Das ist eine alte Kirche in Hamburg; Hier bin ich, ich esse eine Brezel

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: adapting a text such as a story, and presenting it to a younger audience, for example, changing the gender or age of the main character; changing the place or time of the setting; adding a new character or dilemma

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: role-playing characters from different areas in German-speaking communities and demonstrating regional variations in language use, for example, in greetings such as the Swiss Grüezi and Austrian or Bavarian Servus, and cultural events such as the Weihnachtsmarkt and the Christkindlmarkt

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and performing a new version of a familiar song or poem, for example, using secure digital tools and apps for video editing and voice recording

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: inventing a board game focusing on key language and using expressions for playing games, for example, Du bist dran; Schade; Gut gemacht; Ich gewinne

as_extracts.name: LGERF106-E02

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6U01 - German
content_descriptions.text: apply combinations of sounds, syllables, pronunciation and intonation patterns to develop fluency in words, phrases and sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how pitch, stress and rhythm help to convey meaning even if individual words are unfamiliar

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying phonic and grammatical knowledge to spell, write and say unfamiliar words containing, for example, ch, j, w and z, and diphthongs such as au and eu, and ei and ie

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using phrasing and intonation to link multiple sentences when reading a short text aloud or holding a reciprocal conversation with a partner

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying differences in regional accents and dialects to begin understanding language variation across German-speaking communities, for example, watching video clips and identifying the commonalties with other geographically adjacent languages or the potentially different pronunciations of ch in different dialects (e.g. in Technologie and ich)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to the ways a word is said in different dialects, for example, ich is pronounced ‘ick’ in Berlin, ‘isch’ in central Germany, ‘i’ in Bavaria and ‘ich’ in northern Germany, and in Switzerland it becomes very guttural, emphasising the ‘ch’ sound

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating places on a map to identify where accents are from, while listening to one word said in different dialects

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising different intonation for statements, questions, exclamations and instructions, for example, Du trinkst Wasser. / Du trinkst Wasser? / Du trinkst Wasser! / Du, trink Wasser!

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: reciting well-known German tongue twisters, applying knowledge of pronunciation patterns and working on fluency, for example, Zehn Ziegen zogen zehn Zentner Zucker; Acht alte Ameisen

content_descriptions.text: initiate and sustain modelled exchanges in familiar contexts related to their personal worlds and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information with others in a secure, teacher-moderated online environment, in writing or face-to-face, about daily routines and leisure activities, using modelled language associated with time and sequence, for example, Was machst du am Wochenende?; Ich stehe um 7.30 Uhr auf. Dann frühstücke ich.; Ich schwimme und surfe oft; or sharing opinions with German-speaking peers about school subjects and rules, for example, Wie findest du Mathe? Mathe ist toll.; Man muss eine Uniform tragen. Das ist doof. Was denkst du?

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using communication strategies such as active listening skills and interjections (e.g. Ja, ja ich verstehe; Ach ja das stimmt; Genau), turn-taking cues, and requests for clarification or more detail to support interactions (e.g. Ich verstehe das nicht; Wie heißt das auf Englisch?)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising modelled repair strategies, for example, Wie bitte?; Kannst du die Frage nochmal sagen?; Bitte sag das nochmal

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving and receiving instructions, for example, Mach(t) die Tür zu!; Trink(t) mehr Wasser!

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing significant people such as family members, friends and teachers, using simple descriptive and expressive modelled language, for example, Das ist meine Schwester. Sie ist sehr sportlich und intelligent. Sie spielt sehr gern Fußball und liest gern Comics. Ich habe meine Schwester lieb.

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking questions using question words to request further detail, and responding using modelled intonation and stress patterns, for example, Welche Farbe hat dein Haustier?; Wie ist es?; Wo wohnt es?

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising subject–verb inversion of questions (e.g. Er ist zehn Jahre alt / Ist er zehn Jahre alt?)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and discussing learning strengths and experiences, for example, Ich mag Deutsch. Deutsch macht Spaß. Ich lerne gern Deutsch.

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: apologising and expressing concern or sympathy to friends and family members, for example, Tut mir leid; Schade!; Du Arme(r)!

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C01-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing feelings (e.g. Wie geht’s?; Es geht mir nicht gut; Ich bin krank), using adjectives such as aufgeregt, glücklich, nervös, sauer and traurig

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6C02 - German
content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve discussion with others, using language that expresses information, preferences and ideas

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in real-life or role-played transactions such as buying food from a range, for example, Ich esse Käse. Ich nehme ein Käsebrötchen.; Was kostet ein Eis? Das macht 6,50 Euro.; Gibt es Vanilla? Vanilla ist mein Lieblingseis.

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising and conducting collaborative activities such as a Deutsch macht fit session for a younger class, using language such as Lauft schnell! and Springt zehnmal!

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing and planning collaboratively with peers to develop an activity for a school assembly, or a school/class event or performance, using language related to people, items, time and numbers to create promotional materials, for example, working collaboratively to produce a poster or video to encourage recycling (e.g. Trinkt lieber Wasser!; Recycelt alle Dosen!) or dancing the action song ‘Das Fliegerlied’ as a lunchtime flash mob

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: checking on peer progress using comments and questions (e.g. Bist du fertig? Ich bin fertig.; Verstehst du das? Ja.) and sharing ideas about the experience of learning and using German, identifying their own strengths and preferred learning styles, for example, Ich kann gut Deutsch sprechen

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to feedback on a written draft or class activity by making changes to improve the product or activity

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: consulting online catalogues and websites, comparing prices and values, and discussing potential purchases (e.g. Das Handy ist zu teuer; Der Pullover ist preiswert) and using modelled phrases such as Der Hut sieht gut aus

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: stating preferences from a range of items, for example, designing outfits from a clothing catalogue (e.g. Mein Lieblingsoutfit ist lila und weiß)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking peers to do something politely and responding to requests, for example, giving and receiving things (e.g. Gib mir bitte den Stift!; Bitte schön; Danke schön)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing and creating class and school rules using modelled language with the modal verbs müssen and dürfen, for example, Dürfen wir auf dem Boden sitzen?; Wir müssen immer aufpassen; Wir dürfen in der Klasse nicht am Handy sein

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C02-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the exchange rate of currencies, for example, converting Euro or Schweizer Franken into Australian dollars, and calculating the cost of specific items in both currencies

as_extracts.name: LGERF106-E04
as_extracts.description: They use strategies to locate and interpret information and ideas in texts, and demonstrate understanding by responding in German or English, adjusting their responses to context, purpose and audience.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6C03 - German
content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, and respond in different ways to suit purpose
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing or reading informative texts and sequencing steps in a process, for example, watching a short video about the water cycle in German and labelling a diagram with vom Meer zum Land; Regen; Fluss; Grundwasser

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a news item, image or short documentary about a festival in a German-speaking country or region, such as die Basler Fasnacht or der Karneval in Köln, and describing and giving an opinion about the main aspects, for example, Ich finde die Fasnacht in Basel super. Ich mag die Masken und die Musik.

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to a text such as a poem by selecting an appropriate image to illustrate an aspect such as the key message or mood, and explaining choices, for example, Das ist die Sonne. Die Sonne ist heiß und gelb. Die Sonne scheint im Sommer. Ich freue mich, wenn die Sonne scheint.

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching topics (eg. recycling, the water cycle, the solar system, or geographical features in German-speaking countries and regions), using a range of sources (e.g. magazine articles, books or websites), and then organising and sharing the information in print or secure digital format in modelled German texts

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing subtitled media such as music clips or informative texts on different German-speaking communities, and identifying new vocabulary and expressions for use in shared texts

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying information in German texts such as advertisements, dialogues, brochures and announcements, and sharing this information with others in another format, for example, presenting a chart of favourite television programs, leisure activities or food preferences

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C03-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: compiling and presenting information from a survey of peers and displaying results, for example, using graphs showing modes of transport to school (e.g. zu Fuß; mit dem Rad/Bus/Auto; mit der Bahn/Fähre), and reporting whether they are environmentally friendly

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C03-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using modelled structures (e.g. Das Ende war lustig/traurig/blöd; Die Hauptperson war sehr mutig/schön/schlau) to express a personal opinion on aspects of a text such as the beginning, ending, plot and characters

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C03-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing a timeline of main events in a story or creating storyboards to represent key events in different types of imaginative texts, including captions or word bubbles to indicate moods or feelings

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6C04 - German
content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in German in familiar non-verbal, spoken and written contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing how language use reflects politeness and the closeness of social relationships, such as different levels of formality through the use of du/ihr and Sie

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common scaffolded phrases such as using Sie in short role-plays with adults outside the family, including people in a position of authority such as a teacher or doctor, for example, Guten Morgen, wie heißen Sie?

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing familiarity with friends, for example, Spitznamen and various uses of the diminutives -chen and -lein

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying when literal translation is or is not possible, for example, in idiomatic expressions such as Bist du satt? (not voll) and Es geht mir gut (not Ich bin gut), or Ich bin krank, which literally translates to ‘I am sick’

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing and practising the use of German expressions and gestures when interacting with people from German-speaking communities, for example, exclamations such as Ach so!, Echt! and Doch!; pressing thumbs inside one’s fists, compared with crossing one’s fingers for good luck; and the similarity of thumbs up meaning ‘great’ or ‘good’

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using German–English cognates to predict meaning (e.g. Brot, kalt, Maske, trinken)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining in English the use and meaning of German expressions (e.g. Gesundheit; Hals- und Beinbruch; Toi, toi, toi!), and noting equivalents or expressions used in the same circumstances from Australia or other cultures, such as Sie spricht durch die Blume – She’s talking in a roundabout way; or noting that German, like all languages, is constantly expanding to include new words and expressions in response to changing intercultural experiences (e.g. Fast Food; Fairness)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and using bilingual resources for language learning, for example, glossaries or personal German–English and English–German wordlists with examples and explanations of parts of speech and language use

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising long compound words, collecting and analysing interesting examples such as das Schlagzeug, babyleicht and der Seehund, and discussing strategies for understanding and translating them into English

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the gender of compound nouns is determined by the last noun in the chain, for example, die See (ocean) + der Hund (dog) = der Seehund (seal)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6U03 - German
content_descriptions.text: compare German language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using familiar metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discovering some loan words from English and/or other languages used by German speakers (e.g. das Internet; die App; Stopp!; Sorry!), and considering if they are similar to loan words from German used by English speakers

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing familiar English texts with similar texts in German and/or other languages (e.g. video clips of songs or animated short stories), and noting key text-type conventions or ideas such as target audience and style

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the context, purpose and intended audience of a range of familiar texts in German and English (e.g. fairytales, sports reports or recipes), and noticing similarities and differences across the languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noting that the word order in German instructions (e.g. recipes) often has the verb, in infinitive form, at the end of the instruction (e.g. Butter und Zucker schaumig rühren), and comparing this with English recipes, which use the imperative (e.g. Cream the butter and sugar)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading, viewing and/or listening to different digital and other texts with a common topic, and discussing structural and linguistic similarities and differences, for example, comparing print, radio, television and social media announcements for the same event

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: building metalanguage to comment on grammar and vocabulary (e.g. Substantive/Nomen, Verben, Ordinalzahlen, Präpositionen, Fragewörter and groß/klein schreiben), and comparing this with equivalents in English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U03-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the concept of regular and irregular verbs, and noticing that this is a feature of both German and English, for example, sein – ich bin (to be – I am); du bist (you are)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U03-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the meaning of modal verbs (e.g. müssen, sollen, mögen, können) with English equivalents, noting the level of commitment to an action each modal verb indicates

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U03-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the German and Australian ways of writing a postal address, for example, the Hausnummer (house number) appears after the street name in Germany, but before the street name in Australia; the Postleitzahl (postcode) appears before the suburb/town in Germany, but after the suburb/town in Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U03-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: providing feedback to support peers, using metalanguage, for example, editing each other’s written or spoken texts, and justifying their reasons for editing or changing textual elements

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6C05 - German
content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, using a variety of vocabulary, modelled sentence structures and conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and highlighting typical features of a letter or article, labelling different sections (e.g. heading, introduction, body, conclusion, author), and then annotating a text to identify its structure and linguistic features

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying features common to a range of text types (e.g. title, author, and main content organised into paragraphs), and then completing a jigsaw activity using features of various text types, placing fragments of the text into the correct order based on modelled examples

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a multimedia profile for a group of young German speakers or writing a blog entry for a youth website, for example, about Freizeit, Schule or Freunde

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a video clip to present information or ideas to a particular audience, including elements that may be unfamiliar to German-speaking students, for example, a virtual tour of the school or classroom for exchange student groups, which may also demonstrate that Australian students generally wear school uniforms

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting about German-speaking countries and Australia, for example, population statistics and physical size, daily temperatures, types of housing, pet ownership or most popular leisure activities

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording a multimedia presentation or writing a diary about a real or imaginary trip to a German-speaking country or region, incorporating some famous places they visited and cultural experiences, for example, Das ist eine alte Kirche in Hamburg; Hier bin ich, ich esse eine Brezel

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: adapting a text such as a story, and presenting it to a younger audience, for example, changing the gender or age of the main character; changing the place or time of the setting; adding a new character or dilemma

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: role-playing characters from different areas in German-speaking communities and demonstrating regional variations in language use, for example, in greetings such as the Swiss Grüezi and Austrian or Bavarian Servus, and cultural events such as the Weihnachtsmarkt and the Christkindlmarkt

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and performing a new version of a familiar song or poem, for example, using secure digital tools and apps for video editing and voice recording

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: inventing a board game focusing on key language and using expressions for playing games, for example, Du bist dran; Schade; Gut gemacht; Ich gewinne

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6U02 - German
content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a range of modelled grammatical structures to respond to and create simple texts using conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying punctuation rules, including the meaning and use of full stops and commas in ordinal and decimal numbers (e.g. die 3. Klasse; 9,50 Euro); understanding that German numbers invert the comma and full stop compared to English, for example, Es kostet €6,50 (sechs Euro fünfzig) vs. ‘It costs $6.50’; ‘10,200’ in English vs. 10.200 in German; and recognising that ordinal numbers include a full stop (e.g. ‘6th’ in English vs. 6. in German), clarifying that the full stop in the number does not mean the end of a sentence (e.g. Sankt Nikolaustag ist am 6. Dezember)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing distinctive punctuation features of personal correspondence in German (e.g. Lieber Klaus, followed respectively by a lower-case letter to begin the first sentence, unless the first word is a noun

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to a person, place or object using the nominative and accusative forms of the definite and indefinite article (e.g. Ich habe einen Bruder; Der Hund hat den Ball) and when negating using kein and noting the differences in structure from English, for example, Ich habe keinen Bruder, literally, ‘I have no brother’, means ‘I don’t have a brother’

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and understanding the different forms of ‘you’, such as du (singular informal), Sie (singular/plural formal) and ihr (plural informal), for example, Setz dich; Setzen Sie sich; Setzt euch; Was meint ihr?

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: making connections between possessive adjectives and context, for example, mein/e, dein/e, sein/e, ihr/e; Mein/Dein Bruder ist 12; Seine/Ihre Lieblingsfarbe ist blau

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: making comparisons using simple structures and limited forms of modal verbs mögen and können, for example, Sie mag Kricket; Ich kann gut schwimmen; Ich mag Erdbeeren lieber als Kiwis; Ich kann besser laufen als Radfahren

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that German time uses ‘half to’ and not ‘half past’, for example, Die Schule beginnt um halb neun (literally, ‘The school begins at half nine’, i.e. half past eight), and telling the time using the 12-hour clock and including the half hour, such as Die Schule endet um 3.30

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using prepositions such as nach and vor within formulaic expressions to indicate the timing of events, such as nach der Schule or describing locations using simple formulaic prepositional phrases such as im Wasser, in der Luft, auf dem Land or neben dem Tisch

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the meaning of the conjunctions dass and weil, and noticing that the conjugated verb moves to the end of the subordinate clause when they are used, for example, Ich esse einen Apfel, weil ich Hunger habe

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to quantities of people, objects and prices using cardinal numbers up to 100, including length/height/distance (Meter, Kilometer) and area (Quadratmeter, Quadratkilometer), decimals and common fractions, for example, 85,5 Prozent haben eine Katze; Die Tages temperatur liegt bei minus 8 Grad; Ich habe eine Halbschwester; or referring to a date, including the year, for an event such as a birth date, for example, Meine Oma ist am elften April 1956 geboren

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E11 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing current actions using a range of regular and irregular verbs, such as machen, kaufen, bringen, tragen, lesen, sehen, fahren and essen

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E12 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing experiences using the simple past tense of sein, for example, Ich war krank; Der Film war interessant; Es war windig

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E13 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that articles and pronouns change after certain verbs (Ich danke dir), and after particular prepositions associated with location, for example, Wir gehen in die Stadt; Wir sind in der Stadt

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E14 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding questions using warum and responding with a simple sentence, for example, Warum bist du müde? Ich bin krank.

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E15 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing ‘open hide-and-seek’ where students arrange themselves on and around furniture and the seeker states modelled descriptive sentences to release them, for example, Eric sitzt am Tisch; Flora steht vor der Tafel

elaborations.name: VC2LG6U02-E16 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching animals, plants and/or national parks from German-speaking countries and regions, and then creating alphabetical lists of them; playing games based on target vocabulary from class research, such as animals (e.g. der Wolf) and plants (das Edelweiß); arranging content from class research according to specific instructions, or building modelled texts

as_extracts.name: LGERF106-E06
as_extracts.description: They create texts, selecting and using a variety of vocabulary and sentence structures to suit different contexts.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6C05 - German
content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, using a variety of vocabulary, modelled sentence structures and conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and highlighting typical features of a letter or article, labelling different sections (e.g. heading, introduction, body, conclusion, author), and then annotating a text to identify its structure and linguistic features

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying features common to a range of text types (e.g. title, author, and main content organised into paragraphs), and then completing a jigsaw activity using features of various text types, placing fragments of the text into the correct order based on modelled examples

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a multimedia profile for a group of young German speakers or writing a blog entry for a youth website, for example, about Freizeit, Schule or Freunde

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a video clip to present information or ideas to a particular audience, including elements that may be unfamiliar to German-speaking students, for example, a virtual tour of the school or classroom for exchange student groups, which may also demonstrate that Australian students generally wear school uniforms

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting about German-speaking countries and Australia, for example, population statistics and physical size, daily temperatures, types of housing, pet ownership or most popular leisure activities

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording a multimedia presentation or writing a diary about a real or imaginary trip to a German-speaking country or region, incorporating some famous places they visited and cultural experiences, for example, Das ist eine alte Kirche in Hamburg; Hier bin ich, ich esse eine Brezel

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: adapting a text such as a story, and presenting it to a younger audience, for example, changing the gender or age of the main character; changing the place or time of the setting; adding a new character or dilemma

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: role-playing characters from different areas in German-speaking communities and demonstrating regional variations in language use, for example, in greetings such as the Swiss Grüezi and Austrian or Bavarian Servus, and cultural events such as the Weihnachtsmarkt and the Christkindlmarkt

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and performing a new version of a familiar song or poem, for example, using secure digital tools and apps for video editing and voice recording

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C05-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: inventing a board game focusing on key language and using expressions for playing games, for example, Du bist dran; Schade; Gut gemacht; Ich gewinne

as_extracts.description: They apply rules for pronunciation and intonation in spoken language and apply conventions of spelling and punctuation in written language.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG6C04 - German
content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in German in familiar non-verbal, spoken and written contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing how language use reflects politeness and the closeness of social relationships, such as different levels of formality through the use of du/ihr and Sie

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common scaffolded phrases such as using Sie in short role-plays with adults outside the family, including people in a position of authority such as a teacher or doctor, for example, Guten Morgen, wie heißen Sie?

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing familiarity with friends, for example, Spitznamen and various uses of the diminutives -chen and -lein

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying when literal translation is or is not possible, for example, in idiomatic expressions such as Bist du satt? (not voll) and Es geht mir gut (not Ich bin gut), or Ich bin krank, which literally translates to ‘I am sick’

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing and practising the use of German expressions and gestures when interacting with people from German-speaking communities, for example, exclamations such as Ach so!, Echt! and Doch!; pressing thumbs inside one’s fists, compared with crossing one’s fingers for good luck; and the similarity of thumbs up meaning ‘great’ or ‘good’

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using German–English cognates to predict meaning (e.g. Brot, kalt, Maske, trinken)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining in English the use and meaning of German expressions (e.g. Gesundheit; Hals- und Beinbruch; Toi, toi, toi!), and noting equivalents or expressions used in the same circumstances from Australia or other cultures, such as Sie spricht durch die Blume – She’s talking in a roundabout way; or noting that German, like all languages, is constantly expanding to include new words and expressions in response to changing intercultural experiences (e.g. Fast Food; Fairness)

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and using bilingual resources for language learning, for example, glossaries or personal German–English and English–German wordlists with examples and explanations of parts of speech and language use

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising long compound words, collecting and analysing interesting examples such as das Schlagzeug, babyleicht and der Seehund, and discussing strategies for understanding and translating them into English

elaborations.name: VC2LG6C04-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the gender of compound nouns is determined by the last noun in the chain, for example, die See (ocean) + der Hund (dog) = der Seehund (seal)
