as_extracts.name: LGER7108-E03
as_extracts.description: They locate and respond to information in texts and use visual and contextual cues to help make meaning.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM04 - German
content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in familiar spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, responding appropriately to context, purpose and audience
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key expressions and details in conversations and announcements, and using information in new ways, for example, listening to or viewing an interview with a German-speaking person about family and then creating their family tree

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading, viewing and responding to a range of simple texts such as promotional brochures, signs and websites, to obtain and compile information about places, lifestyles and events, for example, information related to homes, schools, leisure activities, climate and geography

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating, collecting, classifying and summarising information from notices, timetables, interviews and announcements, and presenting the findings to others, for example, in a digital visual presentation, poster or wall chart

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: gathering information from informative texts about people, time and activities in German-speaking communities, and using the information, for example, creating a profile or timetable/timeline to show a sequence of activities/events

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting the results of a class survey, for example, creating graphs, making a video and/or writing statements to report their findings on topics such as the range of leisure activities undertaken by classmates; favourite games, television series, food or music; pets; or the amount of time spent on devices

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with imaginative texts by responding to questions about characters, events and ideas, for example, producing a profile of a character or a timeline of the main events

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting images to illustrate a text, and explaining why qualities such as colour and a symbol or emoji reflect the text’s content/mood and affect choice, for example, Er ist sauer; Das Lied ist optimistisch/aggressiv

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: transforming a simple text into another text type, applying key features and conventions of that text type, for example, changing a diary entry to a secure online blog; changing an advertisement into a narrative

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to an imaginative text in various ways, such as giving opinions about the characters and expressing reactions to the text, for example, Ich sehe ein Mädchen; Ich finde das Mädchen sehr lustig; Das Ende ist traurig

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the ways words can be misinterpreted, for example, the naming of the Barwon River in English (Wadawurrung word Parwan for ‘magpie’), or the Yarra River (Wurundjeri term Yarro Yarro, meaning ‘it flows’), and identifying false friends or commonly misunderstood terms and phrases in German that can cause miscommunication

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM05 - German
content_descriptions.text: develop and apply strategies to interpret and respond to German texts, and to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in German in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating short personal texts, identifying words and phrases that can be translated literally and those that cannot, noting the word order, for example, Guten Appetit!; Guten Tag!; Ohrwurm; Er kann gut singen

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that there are different and/or multiple expressions that communicate ideas across cultures, for example, when describing Brot; Klassenfahrt and Wandertag; Karneval, Fasching and Fastnacht

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing German performances such as music video clips or extracts from films, sharing reactions with peers, noticing ideas and discussing cultural aspects that may be interesting

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating public signs from German to English and vice versa, noticing similarities and differences, for example, Einbahnstraße (one-way street) and Sackgasse (dead end, literally ‘sack alley/lane’)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that in public announcements, compared with private conversations on the phone, certain words are pronounced differently or varied slightly to ensure clarity, for example, zwei/zwo

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and using different reference and translation tools such as wordlists, dictionaries and online translators to interpret and convey meaning according to context

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using German–English cognates to predict meaning (e.g. Brot, kalt, Maske, trinken)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that German compound nouns are formed from a combination of smaller words or different parts of speech, for example, das Krankenhaus (hospital) is made up of krank (sick) and das Haus (house); understanding that the gender of compound nouns is determined by the last noun in the chain, for example, die See (ocean) + der Hund (dog) = der Seehund (seal); collecting and analysing interesting examples such as das Schlagzeug, babyleicht and der Seehund; and discussing how best to translate them into English

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that bilingual resources, glossaries and dictionaries use grammatical explanations to categorise words and inform users of their meaning, or noticing how online dictionaries denote the difference between a noun and verb to assist in word selection

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that German, like all languages, is constantly expanding to include new words and expressions in response to changing intercultural experiences (e.g. Fast Food, Fairness), technological terms (e.g. der Computer) and inclusive language (e.g. Guten Morgen, liebe Lernende)

as_extracts.name: LGER7108-E04
as_extracts.description: They respond in German or English, and demonstrate their understanding of context, purpose and audience in texts.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM04 - German
content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in familiar spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, responding appropriately to context, purpose and audience
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key expressions and details in conversations and announcements, and using information in new ways, for example, listening to or viewing an interview with a German-speaking person about family and then creating their family tree

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading, viewing and responding to a range of simple texts such as promotional brochures, signs and websites, to obtain and compile information about places, lifestyles and events, for example, information related to homes, schools, leisure activities, climate and geography

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating, collecting, classifying and summarising information from notices, timetables, interviews and announcements, and presenting the findings to others, for example, in a digital visual presentation, poster or wall chart

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: gathering information from informative texts about people, time and activities in German-speaking communities, and using the information, for example, creating a profile or timetable/timeline to show a sequence of activities/events

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting the results of a class survey, for example, creating graphs, making a video and/or writing statements to report their findings on topics such as the range of leisure activities undertaken by classmates; favourite games, television series, food or music; pets; or the amount of time spent on devices

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with imaginative texts by responding to questions about characters, events and ideas, for example, producing a profile of a character or a timeline of the main events

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting images to illustrate a text, and explaining why qualities such as colour and a symbol or emoji reflect the text’s content/mood and affect choice, for example, Er ist sauer; Das Lied ist optimistisch/aggressiv

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: transforming a simple text into another text type, applying key features and conventions of that text type, for example, changing a diary entry to a secure online blog; changing an advertisement into a narrative

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to an imaginative text in various ways, such as giving opinions about the characters and expressing reactions to the text, for example, Ich sehe ein Mädchen; Ich finde das Mädchen sehr lustig; Das Ende ist traurig

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the ways words can be misinterpreted, for example, the naming of the Barwon River in English (Wadawurrung word Parwan for ‘magpie’), or the Yarra River (Wurundjeri term Yarro Yarro, meaning ‘it flows’), and identifying false friends or commonly misunderstood terms and phrases in German that can cause miscommunication

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8UL02 - German
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that German numbers invert the comma and full stop compared to English, for example, Es kostet €6,50 (sechs Euro fünfzig) vs. ‘It costs $6.50’; In Melbourne leben 5,1 Millionen Menschen in German vs. ‘5.1 million people live in Melbourne’ in English; and playing bingo (with numbers spoken in German, using Komma and Punkt to indicate punctuation)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing punctuation rules in English and German, for example, considering aspects for direct speech; understanding quotation marks for direct speech; understanding the meaning and use of full stops and commas in German ordinal or decimal numbers (e.g. die 8. Klasse; 15.30 Uhr) and using the German quotation marks correctly, „Hallo! Ich bin Peter.“

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying German punctuation for direct speech through highlighting the speech marks within a text (e.g. „Ich bin Heidi.“ or »Ich bin Heidi.«)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating a simple English text into German, changing English punctuation for direct speech to German punctuation, and then transcribing a simple German text from indirect speech to direct speech, adding punctuation for direct speech

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying German capitalisation rules to nouns and pronouns and noticing that the capitalisation of the formal ‘you’ form, Sie, distinguishes it from the sie (she/they) form; selecting the correct personal pronoun for ‘it’ (er/sie/es/ihn) for objects, for example, Woher hast du den Hut? Er ist sehr schön. Ich habe ihn bei … gekauft.

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying sentence structure rules for verb position, including the use of some modal verbs and questions, and noting that the conjugated verb will not move when the sentence does not start with the subject (e.g. Am Nachmittag spiele ich Tennis; Ich kann gut schwimmen), for example, working in pairs to unjumble sentences (colour-coded for additional support, with verbs in green, nouns in red, etc.)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying subject–verb inversion to form questions without question words by highlighting the verbs in a statement, noting that the verb is always in the second position, and then arranging colour-coded words (e.g. verbs in green, nouns in red) into statements and questions, and matching given statements and questions to pictures or verbal cues (e.g. Du hast Geschwister. – Hast du Geschwister?)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how to create textual cohesion by using elements such as coordinating conjunctions (e.g. und, aber, oder) to link ideas, for example, combining 2 simple sentences to make one complex sentence; separating a complex sentence into 2 simple sentences by identifying the conjunction

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using elements such as simple subordinating conjunctions (e.g. weil) to create textual cohesion, noting the change in word order (the conjugated verb goes to the end), by combining 2 simple sentences to make one complex sentence; or separating a complex sentence into 2 simple sentences by identifying the conjunction and rearranging the word order of the subordinate clause

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising different registers such as the different words for ‘you’ (e.g. Was machst du, Peter?; Was macht ihr, Kinder?; Setz dich, Peter!; Setzt euch Kinder!; Kommen Sie bitte herein, Herr Berger!) by ticking the correct box in a table, or changing a given sentence to match the context and register of images

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E11 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing a basic knowledge of the German case system through modelling of simple ‘subject + verb, + object’ sentences to indicate ‘nominative + verb + accusative’, for example, Ich mag Deutsch; Wir essen Spaghettieis

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E12 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: incorporating the dative case through commonly used phrases such as Wie geht es dir? and Mir geht es gut

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E13 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying definite and indefinite articles in simple sentences or texts and using them in their own writing, for example, highlighting the indefinite article in a paragraph about a pet, and then using this modelled language to write a paragraph about their own pet

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E14 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using personal pronouns (e.g. er, sie, es) and possessive adjectives (e.g. ihr, sein, unser) through modelled sentences in which the pronoun replaces the noun (e.g. Das Haus ist groß / Ein Haus ist groß / Ihr Haus ist groß; Der Hund ist klein / Er ist klein / Mein Hund ist klein; Eric isst ein Brezel. Sein Brezel ist lecker.)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E15 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing current and recurring actions, selecting and conjugating some frequently used regular and irregular verbs (e.g. Ich trinke Orangensaft; Sie isst einen Apfel), by matching captions to pictures, completing cloze or information-gap activities, selecting pronoun–verb combinations from conjugation tables and creating their own sentences, or other activities focusing on pronoun–verb agreement

as_extracts.name: LGER7108-E05
as_extracts.description: They use familiar language, modelled sentences and grammatical structures to create texts appropriate to audience.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM03 - German
content_descriptions.text: engage in modelled spoken and written exchanges with peers to organise activities relating to daily life and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in real-life or role-played situations such as buying a bus/cinema ticket or food, for example, Ich nehme ein Käsebrötchen; Was kostet ein Eis?; Das macht 6,50 Euro

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with peers to produce a bilingual publicity flyer for an upcoming event or performance to promote German language learning among school community members, for example, a German-speaking community day, a language school assembly, or an infographic to introduce a new or improved recycling program at school

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in scenarios such as being lost and asking for directions, and giving directions or assistance, including non-verbal gestures, for example, Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof?; Wo ist die Post?; Geh nach links!; Ich brauche Hilfe!

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in collaborative projects, for example, making and playing a vocabulary game such as Domino, Memory or Quartett, or producing and sharing a digital alphabet or number book for a younger audience

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning for a class celebration, for example, creating an invitation or program using Wann?; Was?; Wer?; Wo?, and then accepting or declining an invitation, for example, using a short message (e.g. Liebe/r X, danke für deine Einladung. Ich kann am Freitag nicht mitkommen. Ich habe Basketballtraining.), or indicating with hand gestures (thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no) whether they are accepting or declining an invitation, based on short responses such as Danke für deine Einladung. Ich kann am Freitag nicht mitkommen.

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a shopping list, such as for a Geburtstagsparty

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating their understanding of texts by drawing items written in German (e.g. animals, party items, hobbies)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating from a continuum of faces (sad face for don’t like; one smiley face for like; 3 smiley faces for favourite) whether speakers like or don’t like something, such as a school subject (e.g. Ich habe Mathe nicht gern – sad face; Ich mag Englisch – one smiley face; Deutsch ist mein Lieblingsfach – 3 smiley faces) or food (e.g. Er isst gern Spaghetti – one smiley face; Sein Lieblingsessen ist Pizza – 3 smiley faces; Er isst nicht gern Gemüse – sad face)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating with others such as students from a partner school to design a bilingual resource, making choices about when to use German or English depending on the context, audience, topic and nature of the interaction, for example, maintaining a website, newsletter, blog or secure digital communication space

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: holding up their fingers to indicate numbers from zero to 10 that are presented on flashcards or stated in simple sentences (e.g. Meine Schwester ist acht Jahre alt – 8 fingers)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM06 - German
content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using appropriate vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures, and some textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information in different formats for different audiences, for example, using a personal text to write an email to a penfriend in a German-speaking country or to introduce a new student to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information in different formats for different audiences, for example, writing an informative text to present statistics related to German-speaking countries and regions or writing a persuasive text to advertise an event

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using different modes of presentation to report on events in their personal worlds, or people or places related to German-speaking communities, such as a multimedia presentation or podcast, a flyer about a community event or a digital travel itinerary

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: compiling a list of questions and conducting an interview, for example, interviewing a German-speaking visitor about their family, home, interests and skills, and presenting the responses in a Steckbrief format, podcast or newsletter

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and presenting an imaginative story or description from a stimulus such as a photograph, and using secure digital tools to create speech bubbles, voice recordings, subtitles or captions to accompany the visuals

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a short play or video clip to share with and entertain others, incorporating actions and props to enhance meaning and to entertain, for example, singing a song or performing a role-play at a school assembly or open day for younger students

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing and participating in imaginary interactions, for example, meeting a character from a German-language story or film for the first time

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing and making bilingual texts or signs for specific audiences, noticing how meaning needs to be tailored for varied audiences and cultural perspectives, for example, a ‘Big Book’ or game for young learners of German; school signage such as Sporthalle and Bibliothek/Bücherei

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting class information to German-speaking students, explaining cultural backgrounds, languages used in the home, interests and hobbies, behavioural expectations, and values, using resources such as photos, captions, quotes and symbols

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8UL01 - German
content_descriptions.text: recognise and apply the sounds and conventions of spoken German to develop fluency, and to respond to and create simple texts in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the pronunciation of particular sounds, rhythms and intonation patterns, for example, reciting tongue twisters, rhymes and short poems such as Fischers Fritze fischt frische Fische; Acht alte Ameisen; Klein aber fein!; ‘Eins, zwei, Polizei’

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying differences in intonation and rhythm between statements, questions, interjections and commands, and, in pairs, practising saying and identifying these, for example, Du trinkst Wasser. / Du trinkst Wasser? / Du trinkst Wasser! / Du, trink Wasser!

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing pronunciation and variation in some letters, for example, singing ‘das Alphabetlied’; using the alphabet to spell German names and other words; recognising that loan words in German may differ in pronunciation or follow the pronunciation patterns of other languages (e.g. Handy, Orange, Friseur, Restaurant); and discussing the linguistic and historical origins of these words

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing short video clips, recognising and understanding that pronunciation may vary across different German-speaking communities and dialects

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing a map of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages with German-speaking countries, noting that the boundaries for languages do not necessarily relate directly to state borders or other modern geopolitical divisions

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing an awareness of letter–sound relationships, including distinctive sounds, such as those represented by the letters ch, r, th, u and z and consonant blends and clusters (e.g. sch), and practising spelling words with these sounds

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that the Eszett, ß, lengthens the preceding vowel

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and applying German sounds, such as short and long vowel sounds (e.g. Maße/Masse) with the support of images to demonstrate underlying concepts

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the sounds of diphthongs (au, eu) in German by listening to the beginning and ending vowels at slow speed

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing common vowel combinations (e.g. ei, ie) and diphthongs (e.g. au, eu) by listening to groups of words, and then placing them in the correct columns of a table based on the sounds heard from the teacher or in an audio clip

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E11 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that the pronunciation of the Umlaut letters ä, ö and ü is distinct from the pronunciation of a, o and u

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E12 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the sounds of the Umlaut letters ä, ö and ü by identifying that they come from the front and top of the mouth, whereas the vowels a, o and u come from the back of the throat

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E13 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing different actions depending on the sound heard, for example, jumping when they hear sch and crouching when they hear ch

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E14 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: singing in a ‘vowel choir’, where students are grouped according to the first vowel in their name and guided by the teacher with hand signals to sing high, low, loudly, softly, a continuous note or a pulsing note

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E15 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the 4 distinctive letters in the German alphabet, ä, ö, ü and ß, are additional to the 26 letters shared with the English alphabet

elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the sounds of diphthongs (au, eu) in German by listening to the beginning and ending vowels at slow speed

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing common vowel combinations (e.g. ei, ie) and diphthongs (e.g. au, eu) by listening to groups of words, and then placing them in the correct columns of a table based on the sounds heard from the teacher or in an audio clip

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E11 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that the pronunciation of the Umlaut letters ä, ö and ü is distinct from the pronunciation of a, o and u

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E12 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the sounds of the Umlaut letters ä, ö and ü by identifying that they come from the front and top of the mouth, whereas the vowels a, o and u come from the back of the throat

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E13 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing different actions depending on the sound heard, for example, jumping when they hear sch and crouching when they hear ch

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E14 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: singing in a ‘vowel choir’, where students are grouped according to the first vowel in their name and guided by the teacher with hand signals to sing high, low, loudly, softly, a continuous note or a pulsing note

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E15 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the 4 distinctive letters in the German alphabet, ä, ö, ü and ß, are additional to the 26 letters shared with the English alphabet

as_extracts.name: LGER7108-E07
as_extracts.description: They demonstrate understanding that German has conventions for non-verbal, spoken and written communication.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM03 - German
content_descriptions.text: engage in modelled spoken and written exchanges with peers to organise activities relating to daily life and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in real-life or role-played situations such as buying a bus/cinema ticket or food, for example, Ich nehme ein Käsebrötchen; Was kostet ein Eis?; Das macht 6,50 Euro

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with peers to produce a bilingual publicity flyer for an upcoming event or performance to promote German language learning among school community members, for example, a German-speaking community day, a language school assembly, or an infographic to introduce a new or improved recycling program at school

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in scenarios such as being lost and asking for directions, and giving directions or assistance, including non-verbal gestures, for example, Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof?; Wo ist die Post?; Geh nach links!; Ich brauche Hilfe!

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in collaborative projects, for example, making and playing a vocabulary game such as Domino, Memory or Quartett, or producing and sharing a digital alphabet or number book for a younger audience

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning for a class celebration, for example, creating an invitation or program using Wann?; Was?; Wer?; Wo?, and then accepting or declining an invitation, for example, using a short message (e.g. Liebe/r X, danke für deine Einladung. Ich kann am Freitag nicht mitkommen. Ich habe Basketballtraining.), or indicating with hand gestures (thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no) whether they are accepting or declining an invitation, based on short responses such as Danke für deine Einladung. Ich kann am Freitag nicht mitkommen.

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a shopping list, such as for a Geburtstagsparty

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating their understanding of texts by drawing items written in German (e.g. animals, party items, hobbies)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating from a continuum of faces (sad face for don’t like; one smiley face for like; 3 smiley faces for favourite) whether speakers like or don’t like something, such as a school subject (e.g. Ich habe Mathe nicht gern – sad face; Ich mag Englisch – one smiley face; Deutsch ist mein Lieblingsfach – 3 smiley faces) or food (e.g. Er isst gern Spaghetti – one smiley face; Sein Lieblingsessen ist Pizza – 3 smiley faces; Er isst nicht gern Gemüse – sad face)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating with others such as students from a partner school to design a bilingual resource, making choices about when to use German or English depending on the context, audience, topic and nature of the interaction, for example, maintaining a website, newsletter, blog or secure digital communication space

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: holding up their fingers to indicate numbers from zero to 10 that are presented on flashcards or stated in simple sentences (e.g. Meine Schwester ist acht Jahre alt – 8 fingers)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM04 - German
content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in familiar spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, responding appropriately to context, purpose and audience
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key expressions and details in conversations and announcements, and using information in new ways, for example, listening to or viewing an interview with a German-speaking person about family and then creating their family tree

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading, viewing and responding to a range of simple texts such as promotional brochures, signs and websites, to obtain and compile information about places, lifestyles and events, for example, information related to homes, schools, leisure activities, climate and geography

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating, collecting, classifying and summarising information from notices, timetables, interviews and announcements, and presenting the findings to others, for example, in a digital visual presentation, poster or wall chart

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: gathering information from informative texts about people, time and activities in German-speaking communities, and using the information, for example, creating a profile or timetable/timeline to show a sequence of activities/events

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting the results of a class survey, for example, creating graphs, making a video and/or writing statements to report their findings on topics such as the range of leisure activities undertaken by classmates; favourite games, television series, food or music; pets; or the amount of time spent on devices

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with imaginative texts by responding to questions about characters, events and ideas, for example, producing a profile of a character or a timeline of the main events

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting images to illustrate a text, and explaining why qualities such as colour and a symbol or emoji reflect the text’s content/mood and affect choice, for example, Er ist sauer; Das Lied ist optimistisch/aggressiv

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: transforming a simple text into another text type, applying key features and conventions of that text type, for example, changing a diary entry to a secure online blog; changing an advertisement into a narrative

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to an imaginative text in various ways, such as giving opinions about the characters and expressing reactions to the text, for example, Ich sehe ein Mädchen; Ich finde das Mädchen sehr lustig; Das Ende ist traurig

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the ways words can be misinterpreted, for example, the naming of the Barwon River in English (Wadawurrung word Parwan for ‘magpie’), or the Yarra River (Wurundjeri term Yarro Yarro, meaning ‘it flows’), and identifying false friends or commonly misunderstood terms and phrases in German that can cause miscommunication

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM06 - German
content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using appropriate vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures, and some textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information in different formats for different audiences, for example, using a personal text to write an email to a penfriend in a German-speaking country or to introduce a new student to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information in different formats for different audiences, for example, writing an informative text to present statistics related to German-speaking countries and regions or writing a persuasive text to advertise an event

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using different modes of presentation to report on events in their personal worlds, or people or places related to German-speaking communities, such as a multimedia presentation or podcast, a flyer about a community event or a digital travel itinerary

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: compiling a list of questions and conducting an interview, for example, interviewing a German-speaking visitor about their family, home, interests and skills, and presenting the responses in a Steckbrief format, podcast or newsletter

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and presenting an imaginative story or description from a stimulus such as a photograph, and using secure digital tools to create speech bubbles, voice recordings, subtitles or captions to accompany the visuals

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a short play or video clip to share with and entertain others, incorporating actions and props to enhance meaning and to entertain, for example, singing a song or performing a role-play at a school assembly or open day for younger students

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing and participating in imaginary interactions, for example, meeting a character from a German-language story or film for the first time

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing and making bilingual texts or signs for specific audiences, noticing how meaning needs to be tailored for varied audiences and cultural perspectives, for example, a ‘Big Book’ or game for young learners of German; school signage such as Sporthalle and Bibliothek/Bücherei

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM06-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting class information to German-speaking students, explaining cultural backgrounds, languages used in the home, interests and hobbies, behavioural expectations, and values, using resources such as photos, captions, quotes and symbols

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8UL01 - German
content_descriptions.text: recognise and apply the sounds and conventions of spoken German to develop fluency, and to respond to and create simple texts in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the pronunciation of particular sounds, rhythms and intonation patterns, for example, reciting tongue twisters, rhymes and short poems such as Fischers Fritze fischt frische Fische; Acht alte Ameisen; Klein aber fein!; ‘Eins, zwei, Polizei’

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying differences in intonation and rhythm between statements, questions, interjections and commands, and, in pairs, practising saying and identifying these, for example, Du trinkst Wasser. / Du trinkst Wasser? / Du trinkst Wasser! / Du, trink Wasser!

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing pronunciation and variation in some letters, for example, singing ‘das Alphabetlied’; using the alphabet to spell German names and other words; recognising that loan words in German may differ in pronunciation or follow the pronunciation patterns of other languages (e.g. Handy, Orange, Friseur, Restaurant); and discussing the linguistic and historical origins of these words

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing short video clips, recognising and understanding that pronunciation may vary across different German-speaking communities and dialects

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing a map of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages with German-speaking countries, noting that the boundaries for languages do not necessarily relate directly to state borders or other modern geopolitical divisions

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing an awareness of letter–sound relationships, including distinctive sounds, such as those represented by the letters ch, r, th, u and z and consonant blends and clusters (e.g. sch), and practising spelling words with these sounds

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that the Eszett, ß, lengthens the preceding vowel

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and applying German sounds, such as short and long vowel sounds (e.g. Maße/Masse) with the support of images to demonstrate underlying concepts

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the sounds of diphthongs (au, eu) in German by listening to the beginning and ending vowels at slow speed

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing common vowel combinations (e.g. ei, ie) and diphthongs (e.g. au, eu) by listening to groups of words, and then placing them in the correct columns of a table based on the sounds heard from the teacher or in an audio clip

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E11 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that the pronunciation of the Umlaut letters ä, ö and ü is distinct from the pronunciation of a, o and u

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E12 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising the sounds of the Umlaut letters ä, ö and ü by identifying that they come from the front and top of the mouth, whereas the vowels a, o and u come from the back of the throat

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E13 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing different actions depending on the sound heard, for example, jumping when they hear sch and crouching when they hear ch

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E14 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: singing in a ‘vowel choir’, where students are grouped according to the first vowel in their name and guided by the teacher with hand signals to sing high, low, loudly, softly, a continuous note or a pulsing note

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL01-E15 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the 4 distinctive letters in the German alphabet, ä, ö, ü and ß, are additional to the 26 letters shared with the English alphabet

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8UL02 - German
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that German numbers invert the comma and full stop compared to English, for example, Es kostet €6,50 (sechs Euro fünfzig) vs. ‘It costs $6.50’; In Melbourne leben 5,1 Millionen Menschen in German vs. ‘5.1 million people live in Melbourne’ in English; and playing bingo (with numbers spoken in German, using Komma and Punkt to indicate punctuation)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing punctuation rules in English and German, for example, considering aspects for direct speech; understanding quotation marks for direct speech; understanding the meaning and use of full stops and commas in German ordinal or decimal numbers (e.g. die 8. Klasse; 15.30 Uhr) and using the German quotation marks correctly, „Hallo! Ich bin Peter.“

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying German punctuation for direct speech through highlighting the speech marks within a text (e.g. „Ich bin Heidi.“ or »Ich bin Heidi.«)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating a simple English text into German, changing English punctuation for direct speech to German punctuation, and then transcribing a simple German text from indirect speech to direct speech, adding punctuation for direct speech

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying German capitalisation rules to nouns and pronouns and noticing that the capitalisation of the formal ‘you’ form, Sie, distinguishes it from the sie (she/they) form; selecting the correct personal pronoun for ‘it’ (er/sie/es/ihn) for objects, for example, Woher hast du den Hut? Er ist sehr schön. Ich habe ihn bei … gekauft.

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying sentence structure rules for verb position, including the use of some modal verbs and questions, and noting that the conjugated verb will not move when the sentence does not start with the subject (e.g. Am Nachmittag spiele ich Tennis; Ich kann gut schwimmen), for example, working in pairs to unjumble sentences (colour-coded for additional support, with verbs in green, nouns in red, etc.)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying subject–verb inversion to form questions without question words by highlighting the verbs in a statement, noting that the verb is always in the second position, and then arranging colour-coded words (e.g. verbs in green, nouns in red) into statements and questions, and matching given statements and questions to pictures or verbal cues (e.g. Du hast Geschwister. – Hast du Geschwister?)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how to create textual cohesion by using elements such as coordinating conjunctions (e.g. und, aber, oder) to link ideas, for example, combining 2 simple sentences to make one complex sentence; separating a complex sentence into 2 simple sentences by identifying the conjunction

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using elements such as simple subordinating conjunctions (e.g. weil) to create textual cohesion, noting the change in word order (the conjugated verb goes to the end), by combining 2 simple sentences to make one complex sentence; or separating a complex sentence into 2 simple sentences by identifying the conjunction and rearranging the word order of the subordinate clause

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising different registers such as the different words for ‘you’ (e.g. Was machst du, Peter?; Was macht ihr, Kinder?; Setz dich, Peter!; Setzt euch Kinder!; Kommen Sie bitte herein, Herr Berger!) by ticking the correct box in a table, or changing a given sentence to match the context and register of images

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E11 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing a basic knowledge of the German case system through modelling of simple ‘subject + verb, + object’ sentences to indicate ‘nominative + verb + accusative’, for example, Ich mag Deutsch; Wir essen Spaghettieis

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E12 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: incorporating the dative case through commonly used phrases such as Wie geht es dir? and Mir geht es gut

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E13 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying definite and indefinite articles in simple sentences or texts and using them in their own writing, for example, highlighting the indefinite article in a paragraph about a pet, and then using this modelled language to write a paragraph about their own pet

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E14 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using personal pronouns (e.g. er, sie, es) and possessive adjectives (e.g. ihr, sein, unser) through modelled sentences in which the pronoun replaces the noun (e.g. Das Haus ist groß / Ein Haus ist groß / Ihr Haus ist groß; Der Hund ist klein / Er ist klein / Mein Hund ist klein; Eric isst ein Brezel. Sein Brezel ist lecker.)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E15 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing current and recurring actions, selecting and conjugating some frequently used regular and irregular verbs (e.g. Ich trinke Orangensaft; Sie isst einen Apfel), by matching captions to pictures, completing cloze or information-gap activities, selecting pronoun–verb combinations from conjugation tables and creating their own sentences, or other activities focusing on pronoun–verb agreement

as_extracts.name: LGER7108-E08
as_extracts.description: They comment on aspects of German and English language structures and features, using some metalanguage.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM05 - German
content_descriptions.text: develop and apply strategies to interpret and respond to German texts, and to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in German in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating short personal texts, identifying words and phrases that can be translated literally and those that cannot, noting the word order, for example, Guten Appetit!; Guten Tag!; Ohrwurm; Er kann gut singen

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that there are different and/or multiple expressions that communicate ideas across cultures, for example, when describing Brot; Klassenfahrt and Wandertag; Karneval, Fasching and Fastnacht

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing German performances such as music video clips or extracts from films, sharing reactions with peers, noticing ideas and discussing cultural aspects that may be interesting

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating public signs from German to English and vice versa, noticing similarities and differences, for example, Einbahnstraße (one-way street) and Sackgasse (dead end, literally ‘sack alley/lane’)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that in public announcements, compared with private conversations on the phone, certain words are pronounced differently or varied slightly to ensure clarity, for example, zwei/zwo

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and using different reference and translation tools such as wordlists, dictionaries and online translators to interpret and convey meaning according to context

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using German–English cognates to predict meaning (e.g. Brot, kalt, Maske, trinken)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that German compound nouns are formed from a combination of smaller words or different parts of speech, for example, das Krankenhaus (hospital) is made up of krank (sick) and das Haus (house); understanding that the gender of compound nouns is determined by the last noun in the chain, for example, die See (ocean) + der Hund (dog) = der Seehund (seal); collecting and analysing interesting examples such as das Schlagzeug, babyleicht and der Seehund; and discussing how best to translate them into English

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that bilingual resources, glossaries and dictionaries use grammatical explanations to categorise words and inform users of their meaning, or noticing how online dictionaries denote the difference between a noun and verb to assist in word selection

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that German, like all languages, is constantly expanding to include new words and expressions in response to changing intercultural experiences (e.g. Fast Food, Fairness), technological terms (e.g. der Computer) and inclusive language (e.g. Guten Morgen, liebe Lernende)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E11 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing a basic knowledge of the German case system through modelling of simple ‘subject + verb, + object’ sentences to indicate ‘nominative + verb + accusative’, for example, Ich mag Deutsch; Wir essen Spaghettieis

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E12 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: incorporating the dative case through commonly used phrases such as Wie geht es dir? and Mir geht es gut

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E13 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying definite and indefinite articles in simple sentences or texts and using them in their own writing, for example, highlighting the indefinite article in a paragraph about a pet, and then using this modelled language to write a paragraph about their own pet

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E14 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using personal pronouns (e.g. er, sie, es) and possessive adjectives (e.g. ihr, sein, unser) through modelled sentences in which the pronoun replaces the noun (e.g. Das Haus ist groß / Ein Haus ist groß / Ihr Haus ist groß; Der Hund ist klein / Er ist klein / Mein Hund ist klein; Eric isst ein Brezel. Sein Brezel ist lecker.)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL02-E15 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing current and recurring actions, selecting and conjugating some frequently used regular and irregular verbs (e.g. Ich trinke Orangensaft; Sie isst einen Apfel), by matching captions to pictures, completing cloze or information-gap activities, selecting pronoun–verb combinations from conjugation tables and creating their own sentences, or other activities focusing on pronoun–verb agreement

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8UL03 - German
content_descriptions.text: compare the structures and features of German with English and/or other languages using some metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and explaining aspects of German language and culture that are interesting and/or different when compared with texts in English and/or other languages, for example, answering the phone with their name

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the concept of regular and irregular verbs (e.g. spielen and lesen), and noticing that this is a feature of both German and English as well as other languages such as Italian and Spanish

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: consolidating pronoun–verb agreement by competing against a partner to match cards with singular and plural verb conjugations to their relevant pronouns, and then identifying the conjugation pattern

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that in German a ‘subject + verb’ construction can have multiple English translations (e.g. wir spielen can mean ‘we play’, ‘we are playing’, ‘we do play’, ‘we shall/will play’ and ‘we’re going to play’) by translating simple stories and identifying various contexts in which each translation would be most appropriate, and then formulating German sentences that reflect the multiple translation options in English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and analysing the purpose, intended audience and key features of familiar texts such as signs, instructions, postcards, advertisements, songs and conversations in German, and comparing these with texts in English

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing written and spoken modes of a particular language function in German, English and/or other languages, noticing the language structures used and the varying levels of formality, for example, in an invitation

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL03-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the pluralisation of nouns in German, English and/or other languages, for example, the use of die for all plural nouns, regardless of the gender of singular nouns, and differing ending patterns for plurals (e.g. Maus, Mäuse; Katze, Katzen; game, games; child, children); practising singular and plural nouns by working with a partner to match words to pictures and then identifying the rule

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL03-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that English grammar was previously more closely aligned with German grammar, and that English has changed over time, for example, recognising the link between ‘What thinkest thou?’ in Middle English and Was denkst du? in German, and recognising that German continues to evolve, just as English and other languages do, by researching or discussing examples of how language has changed over time

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL03-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that languages are dynamic and borrow and adapt words and expressions from each other (e.g. English has borrowed from German for hamburger, kaputt, kindergarten and glockenspiel; German has borrowed from English for das Internet, die App, joggen, shoppen, Stopp! and Sorry!); comparing how these words are pronounced by speakers of German, English and/or other languages; and noticing that German and English share many words (e.g. Computer, Bus, Taxi, Auto), and recognising that this is a result of historical events, as well as the evolving nature of language

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL03-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the concept of diversity in accents, dialects and vocabulary in German-speaking communities, as well as in the use of English and/or other languages within and beyond Australia

as_extracts.name: LGER7108-E09
as_extracts.description: They understand how aspects of language and culture contribute to their own and others’ identity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM05 - German
content_descriptions.text: develop and apply strategies to interpret and respond to German texts, and to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in German in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating short personal texts, identifying words and phrases that can be translated literally and those that cannot, noting the word order, for example, Guten Appetit!; Guten Tag!; Ohrwurm; Er kann gut singen

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that there are different and/or multiple expressions that communicate ideas across cultures, for example, when describing Brot; Klassenfahrt and Wandertag; Karneval, Fasching and Fastnacht

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing German performances such as music video clips or extracts from films, sharing reactions with peers, noticing ideas and discussing cultural aspects that may be interesting

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating public signs from German to English and vice versa, noticing similarities and differences, for example, Einbahnstraße (one-way street) and Sackgasse (dead end, literally ‘sack alley/lane’)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that in public announcements, compared with private conversations on the phone, certain words are pronounced differently or varied slightly to ensure clarity, for example, zwei/zwo

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and using different reference and translation tools such as wordlists, dictionaries and online translators to interpret and convey meaning according to context

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using German–English cognates to predict meaning (e.g. Brot, kalt, Maske, trinken)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that German compound nouns are formed from a combination of smaller words or different parts of speech, for example, das Krankenhaus (hospital) is made up of krank (sick) and das Haus (house); understanding that the gender of compound nouns is determined by the last noun in the chain, for example, die See (ocean) + der Hund (dog) = der Seehund (seal); collecting and analysing interesting examples such as das Schlagzeug, babyleicht and der Seehund; and discussing how best to translate them into English

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that bilingual resources, glossaries and dictionaries use grammatical explanations to categorise words and inform users of their meaning, or noticing how online dictionaries denote the difference between a noun and verb to assist in word selection

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM05-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that German, like all languages, is constantly expanding to include new words and expressions in response to changing intercultural experiences (e.g. Fast Food, Fairness), technological terms (e.g. der Computer) and inclusive language (e.g. Guten Morgen, liebe Lernende)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8UL04 - German
content_descriptions.text: recognise how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the impact of their own assumptions about people from German-speaking countries and regions, their language and their culture, and considering how German speakers may similarly make assumptions and generalisations about Australia and people living in Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a ‘language portrait’ of themselves through the use of a whole-body silhouette, where students represent their personal experiences of language and culture by adding colours, shapes and words within and around the outline

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL04-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing interactions between German-speaking people in different contexts, noticing and recording elements that reflect cultural attitudes or behaviours, such as language associated with politeness or emotion, gift-giving customs, or ways of showing collective appreciation or approval, for example, applauding by rapping on the surface of a table or stating Bitte schön; Entschuldigung; Wie schön!; Ich danke dir!, or reflecting on the relationship between language, culture and behaviour, and comparing these with English and other languages, for example, considering the use of family names with titles (e.g. Guten Tag, Frau Stein and formal/informal register du/ihr/Sie)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL04-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding their own cultural and linguistic heritage and its role in shaping identity, for example, annotating a family tree with information about family members, highlighting significant places or languages spoken using modelled language such as Ich bin Australier/-in. Mein Opa kommt aus Griechenland

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL04-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the use and cultural significance of body language, including gestures in German and other languages, and selecting those that can be easily incorporated into interactions when communicating in German, for example, shaking hands as a common greeting, and maintaining eye contact when appropriate

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL04-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in cultural experiences and reflecting on cultural similarities and differences, for example, eating at a German/Swiss/Austrian restaurant or café in Australia or watching a German music performance, soccer match or skiing competition; or examining examples of cultural representation in language, symbols and behaviour, such as die Märchenstraße, the lack of speed limits on the Autobahn, national and state flags or coats of arms, and the visibility of the European Union through placement of its logo (e.g. on car numberplates)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL04-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a guided discussion and comparing aspects of identity that may be important across cultures, such as state, country, ethnic group, language, religion, age, preferred gender, position in family, Heimatland and Festtage

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL04-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating connections between language and significant cultural values or practices in Australia and German-speaking communities, such as individual rights, shared social responsibility, respect for the environment, and anti-racism

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV2
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews are formed by different experiences at a personal, local, national and global level, and are linked to individual, community and political mandates and actions for sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL04-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring how origin, geography and religion are directly connected to lifestyle, daily practices and language use, for example, Recycling; Kaffee und Kuchen; Wandern; religious/public holidays; or the choice of Fremdsprachen offered in schools, at what year level it is introduced and how it is taught

elaborations.name: VC2LG8UL04-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and locating countries and regions on a world map where German is the official language or a co-official language (i.e. Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Belgium, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg and South Tyrol), and gaining an awareness of some regional variations in language, for example, in greetings such as the Swiss Grüezi and Austrian or Bavarian Servus, or the lack of the Eszett in Switzerland and Liechtenstein

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM01 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: interact with others using modelled language to exchange information in familiar contexts about themselves and their personal worlds

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM01-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging simple formal/informal greetings, thanks and good wishes using formulaic expressions, adjusting language to suit the situation and time of day, for example, Guten Morgen!; Guten Abend!; Auf Wiedersehen!; Tschüss!; Morgen!; Danke!; Alles Gute zum Geburtstag!; Guten Appetit!; Moin!; Grüezi!; Servus!

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM01-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing and describing themselves, others, and their possessions and relationships, working in pairs (e.g. Ich heiße …; Das ist …; Sie ist nett; Ich bin … Jahre alt und meine Augen sind braun; Ich wohne in ….; Ich komme aus …; Das ist mein Vater / meine Freundin / mein Handy), for example, completing an information-gap activity, listening to their partner’s responses and completing the missing information on their worksheet

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM01-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing and comparing information about themselves and others in formal and informal situations (e.g. Wie heißt du?; Wie heißen Sie?; Wie geht’s?; Wie geht es Ihnen?; Wie alt bist du?; Hast du ein Haustier?; Hast du Geschwister?), for example, participating in role-plays

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM01-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information about their daily routine and life (e.g. Wie kommst du zur Schule? Ich fahre mit dem Bus/Auto.; Wann stehst du auf? Um sechs Uhr.), for example, participating in a ‘Find someone who …’ activity

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM01-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing how they are feeling when their name is called on the roll, for example, Es geht mir nicht gut; Ich bin krank; Ich bin glücklich

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM01-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing and comparing information with German-speaking people about their own and others’ interests, using a conversation or written/secure digital communication, for example, discussing local seasons and foods or popular leisure activities in the area

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM01-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: using appropriate and preferred forms of address and greetings/salutations within different types of correspondence and social contexts, for example, Lieber/Liebe …; Dein/Deine …; Guten Morgen, Herr Schiller!; Hallo, Tim!

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM01-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging details with peers in phone conversations, emails, text messages, notes or letters about the time, date and location of an activity, for example, Wann spielen wir? Wir spielen am Montagnachmittag in der Sporthalle.; Ich gehe am Samstag zum Fußball. Kommst du mit?

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM01-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing likes, dislikes and preferences, for example, Ich mag rot; Mein Lieblingsessen ist …; Ich lese gern; Ich esse gern Pizza, aber ich esse lieber Nudeln

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM01-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising phone etiquette by answering a real or imagined phone call by stating their family name only, and ending the call with Auf Wiederhören

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM02 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: develop language to interact in exchanges, routines and tasks related to their classroom and interests

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM02-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to classroom instructions, for example, Mach das Fenster zu; Stapelt die Stühle; Mach das Licht aus; Auf Deutsch, bitte!

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM02-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing aspects of school life such as timetables, subjects, teachers and uniforms, for example, Wann haben wir montags Deutsch?

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM02-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving their opinions on aspects of school life such as timetables, subjects, teachers and uniforms, for example, Ich finde Mathe interessant, aber meine Mathelehrerin ist sehr streng. Und du, findest du Mathe auch interessant?

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM02-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing progress by asking and answering questions during a class activity, for example, Bist du fertig? Ich bin fertig.; Verstehst du das? Ja.

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM02-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting in class activities and digital games such as Leute-Lotto and Stadt, Land, Fluss, for example, Du bist dran!; Ich gewinne!; Du mogelst!

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM02-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: following procedures and instructions (e.g. Hört zu; Lies … vor; Steht auf!), for example, participating in class or leisure activities such as sport, craft, dance or cooking

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM03 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: engage in modelled spoken and written exchanges with peers to organise activities relating to daily life and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in real-life or role-played situations such as buying a bus/cinema ticket or food, for example, Ich nehme ein Käsebrötchen; Was kostet ein Eis?; Das macht 6,50 Euro

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with peers to produce a bilingual publicity flyer for an upcoming event or performance to promote German language learning among school community members, for example, a German-speaking community day, a language school assembly, or an infographic to introduce a new or improved recycling program at school

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E03 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in scenarios such as being lost and asking for directions, and giving directions or assistance, including non-verbal gestures, for example, Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof?; Wo ist die Post?; Geh nach links!; Ich brauche Hilfe!

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E04 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in collaborative projects, for example, making and playing a vocabulary game such as Domino, Memory or Quartett, or producing and sharing a digital alphabet or number book for a younger audience

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E05 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning for a class celebration, for example, creating an invitation or program using Wann?; Was?; Wer?; Wo?, and then accepting or declining an invitation, for example, using a short message (e.g. Liebe/r X, danke für deine Einladung. Ich kann am Freitag nicht mitkommen. Ich habe Basketballtraining.), or indicating with hand gestures (thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no) whether they are accepting or declining an invitation, based on short responses such as Danke für deine Einladung. Ich kann am Freitag nicht mitkommen.

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E06 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a shopping list, such as for a Geburtstagsparty

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E07 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating their understanding of texts by drawing items written in German (e.g. animals, party items, hobbies)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E08 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: indicating from a continuum of faces (sad face for don’t like; one smiley face for like; 3 smiley faces for favourite) whether speakers like or don’t like something, such as a school subject (e.g. Ich habe Mathe nicht gern – sad face; Ich mag Englisch – one smiley face; Deutsch ist mein Lieblingsfach – 3 smiley faces) or food (e.g. Er isst gern Spaghetti – one smiley face; Sein Lieblingsessen ist Pizza – 3 smiley faces; Er isst nicht gern Gemüse – sad face)

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E09 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating with others such as students from a partner school to design a bilingual resource, making choices about when to use German or English depending on the context, audience, topic and nature of the interaction, for example, maintaining a website, newsletter, blog or secure digital communication space

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM03-E10 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: holding up their fingers to indicate numbers from zero to 10 that are presented on flashcards or stated in simple sentences (e.g. Meine Schwester ist acht Jahre alt – 8 fingers)

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LG8CM04 - German
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in familiar spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, responding appropriately to context, purpose and audience
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E01 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key expressions and details in conversations and announcements, and using information in new ways, for example, listening to or viewing an interview with a German-speaking person about family and then creating their family tree

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E02 - German
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading, viewing and responding to a range of simple texts such as promotional brochures, signs and websites, to obtain and compile information about places, lifestyles and events, for example, information related to homes, schools, leisure activities, climate and geography

elaborations.name: VC2LG8CM04-E03 - German
